bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第064卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 64
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 64

sentences.zh: 【漢紀五十六】　起重光大荒落，盡旃蒙作噩，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Han Records 56] From Chongguang Dahuangluo through Zhanmeng Zuo'e, in all five years.
translations.idiomatic: Han Records 56 — from the year jiaxu (201) through jisi (205), five years in total.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, on the first day of the cycle dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, on the first day of the month (dingmao), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 曹操就谷於安民。

translations.literal: Cao Cao obtained grain at Anmin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao drew provisions at Anmin.

sentences.zh: 以袁紹新破，欲以其間擊劉表。

translations.literal: Because Yuan Shao had just been newly defeated, he wished to use the interval to attack Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuan Shao freshly defeated, he planned to strike Liu Biao while the opportunity lasted.

sentences.zh: 荀彧曰：「紹既新敗，其眾離心，宜乘其困，遂定之。

translations.literal: Xun Yu said: "Yuan Shao has just been newly defeated, and his troops' hearts are divided; you ought to take advantage of his distress and settle matters with him then and there.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, "Yuan Shao has just suffered a crushing defeat and his men are losing heart. You should press him while he is weak and finish him off.

sentences.zh: 而欲遠師江、漢，若紹收其餘燼，承虛以出人後，則公事去矣。

translations.literal: Yet you wish to lead troops far away to the Yangtze and Han; if Yuan Shao gathers his remaining embers and, seizing on your absence, strikes from behind, then the great enterprise will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: But if you march far south to the Yangtze and Han, Yuan Shao may rally his scattered forces and strike at your rear while you are away — and your whole cause will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」操乃止。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，操揚兵河上，擊袁紹倉亭軍，破之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao displayed his troops along the Yellow River, attacked Yuan Shao's army at Cangting, and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao marched along the Yellow River, attacked Yuan Shao's forces at Cangting, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，操還許。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the ninth month, Cao Cao returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, Cao Cao returned to Xu.

sentences.zh: 操自擊劉備於汝南，備奔劉表，龔都等皆散。

translations.literal: Cao Cao himself attacked Liu Bei at Runan; Liu Bei fled to Liu Biao, and Gong Du and the others all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao personally attacked Liu Bei at Runan. Liu Bei fled to Liu Biao, and Gong Du and his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 表聞備至，自出郊迎，以上賓禮待之，益其兵，使屯新野。

translations.literal: When Liu Biao heard that Liu Bei had arrived, he went out to the suburbs to welcome him, treated him with the rites due a supreme guest, increased his troops, and had him garrison at Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao learned that Liu Bei had come, he went out to meet him in person, received him as an honored guest, reinforced his army, and stationed him at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 備在荊州數年，嘗於表坐起至廁，慨然流涕。

translations.literal: Liu Bei had been in Jing Province for several years; once, while rising from Liu Biao's seat to go to the privy, he sighed deeply and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in Jing Province, Liu Bei once rose from Liu Biao's couch to visit the privy and wept openly in distress.

sentences.zh: 表怪，問備，備曰：「平常身不離鞍，髀肉皆消。

translations.literal: Liu Biao was puzzled and asked Liu Bei; Liu Bei said: "In ordinary times my body never left the saddle, and the flesh on my thighs all wasted away.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao was astonished and asked the reason. Liu Bei said, "In the old days I was never off horseback, and the flesh on my thighs wore thin.

sentences.zh: 今不復騎，髀裡肉生。

translations.literal: Now I no longer ride, and flesh has grown again on the inside of my thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Now I ride no more, and flesh has grown back on my thighs.

sentences.zh: 日月如流，老將至矣，而功業不建，是以悲耳。

translations.literal: Days and months flow like a stream; old age is nearly upon me, yet my achievements are not established — that is why I grieve."
translations.idiomatic: The days and months rush past like a stream; old age is upon me, yet I have accomplished nothing — that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 曹操遣夏侯淵、張遼圍昌豨於東海，數月，糧盡，議引軍還。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan and Zhang Liao to besiege Chang Xi in Donghai; after several months their grain was exhausted, and they discussed withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan and Zhang Liao to besiege Chang Xi in Donghai. After several months their supplies ran out, and they debated pulling the army back.

sentences.zh: 遼謂淵曰：「數日已來，每行諸圍，豨輒屬目視遼，又其射矢更稀。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao said to Xiahou Yuan: "For several days now, whenever I pass the various encirclements, Xi keeps fixing his gaze on Liao, and moreover his arrows are shot more sparingly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao said to Xiahou Yuan, "These past few days, whenever I inspect the siege lines, Xi keeps staring at me, and his archers shoot less and less often.

sentences.zh: 此必豨計猶豫，故不力戰。

translations.literal: This must mean that Xi is hesitating in his plans and therefore does not fight with full force.
translations.idiomatic: He must be wavering in his mind and therefore is not fighting with his full strength.

sentences.zh: 遼欲挑與語，倘可誘也。

translations.literal: Liao wishes to provoke conversation with him; perhaps he can be enticed."
translations.idiomatic: I want to draw him into talk — perhaps he can be won over."

sentences.zh: 」乃使謂豨曰：「公有命，使遼傳之。

translations.literal: " He then had someone tell Xi: "The lord has a command and has sent Liao to convey it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent word to Xi: "The lord has orders, and Liao is here to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 」豨果下與遼語。

translations.literal: " Xi indeed came down to speak with Zhang Liao.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi came down from the walls and spoke with Zhang Liao.

sentences.zh: 遼為說操神武，方以德懷四方，先附者受大賞，豨乃許降。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao expounded on Cao Cao's divine martial prowess and how he was just then winning the four quarters through virtue; those who submitted first would receive great rewards, and Xi thereupon agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao spoke of Cao Cao's martial prowess and his policy of winning the realm through virtue, promising rich rewards to those who came over first. Xi agreed to surrender.

sentences.zh: 遼遂單身上三公山，入豨家，拜妻子，豨歡喜，隨遼詣操。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao then went alone up Mount Sangong, entered Xi's home, and bowed to his wife and children; Xi was delighted and followed Zhang Liao to see Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao then went alone up Mount Sangong, entered Xi's home, and paid his respects to Xi's wife and children. Delighted, Xi accompanied Zhang Liao to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操遣豨還。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Xi back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xi back to his post.

sentences.zh: 趙韙圍劉璋於成都。

translations.literal: Zhao Wei besieged Liu Zhang at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wei besieged Liu Zhang at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 東州人恐見誅滅，相與力戰，韙遂敗退，追至江州，殺之。

translations.literal: The men of Dong Province, fearing they would be put to death, joined forces and fought strenuously; Zhao Wei was defeated and retreated, was pursued to Jiangzhou, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongzhou troops, fearing extermination, fought together with desperate force. Zhao Wei was defeated, fled, was pursued to Jiangzhou, and killed.

sentences.zh: 龐羲懼，遣吏程祁宣旨於其父漢昌令畿，索賨兵。

translations.literal: Pang Xi was afraid and sent the clerk Cheng Qi to convey instructions to his father, the magistrate of Hanchang, Ji, demanding the Cong troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xi, in fear, sent the clerk Cheng Qi to his father Ji, magistrate of Hanchang, to demand the Cong tribal levies.

sentences.zh: 畿曰：「郡合部曲，本不為亂，縱有讒諛，要在盡誠，若遂懷異志，不敢聞命。

translations.literal: Ji said: "The commandery's assembled retainers were never raised for rebellion; even if there are slanderers, what matters is to give one's utmost loyalty. If you now harbor a different intent, I dare not hear the command."
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "The commandery's forces were never mustered for rebellion. Even if slanderers speak against us, loyalty is what matters. If you now turn disloyal, I will not obey."

sentences.zh: 」羲更使祁說之，畿曰：「我受牧恩，當為盡節；

translations.literal: " Xi again sent Cheng Qi to persuade him; Ji said: "I have received favor from the governor and ought to give my utmost in loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: " Xi sent Cheng Qi again. Ji said, "I owe the governor a debt of gratitude and must serve him faithfully;

sentences.zh: 汝為郡吏，自宜效力。

translations.literal: you are a commandery clerk and ought yourself to exert your strength.
translations.idiomatic: you are a commandery clerk and ought to do your duty.

sentences.zh: 不義之事，有死不為。

translations.literal: For an unrighteous matter, I would die rather than do it."
translations.idiomatic: For an unrighteous act I would die rather than comply."

sentences.zh: 」羲怒，使人謂畿曰：「不從太守，禍將及家！

translations.literal: " Xi was angry and had someone tell Ji: "If you do not obey the grand administrator, disaster will reach your family!"
translations.idiomatic: " Xi was furious and sent word: "Disobey the grand administrator, and disaster will fall on your whole family!"

sentences.zh: 」畿曰：「樂羊食子，非無父子之恩，大義然也。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "When Yue Yang ate his son, it was not that he lacked the affection between father and son — great righteousness was at stake.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji replied, "When Yue Yang ate his son's flesh, it was not that he lacked fatherly love — duty outweighed affection.

sentences.zh: 今雖羹祁以賜畿，畿啜之矣。

translations.literal: Even if now you were to make a broth of Cheng Qi and present it to Ji, Ji would drink it down."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you boiled Cheng Qi into a stew and served it to me, I would drink it down."

sentences.zh: 」羲乃厚謝於璋。

translations.literal: " Xi thereupon made lavish apologies to Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi then made a full apology to Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 璋擢畿為江陽太守。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang promoted Ji to grand administrator of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang promoted Ji to grand administrator of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞益州亂，以五官中郎將牛但為益州刺史。

translations.literal: When the court heard of the disorder in Yi Province, it appointed the Five Offices Central Gentleman Niu Dan as inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of the turmoil in Yi Province, it appointed Niu Dan, Five Offices Central Gentleman, as inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 征璋為卿，不至。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang was summoned to serve as a minister but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was summoned to court as a minister but did not go.

sentences.zh: 張魯以鬼道教民，使病者自首其過，為之請禱，實無益於治病，然小人昏愚，競共事之。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu used the Way of the Ghosts to teach the people, making the sick confess their transgressions and performing prayers on their behalf; it truly did no good for curing illness, yet petty men, benighted and foolish, all vied to serve him in this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu taught the people through his spirit cult, requiring the sick to confess their sins so he could pray for them. It did nothing to cure disease, yet the simple and credulous flocked to him all the same.

sentences.zh: 犯法者，三原，然後乃行刑。

translations.literal: Those who violated the law were pardoned three times, and only then was punishment carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders were forgiven three times before punishment was imposed.

sentences.zh: 不置長吏，皆以祭酒為治。

translations.literal: He did not appoint regular officials; all governance was entrusted to libationers.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed no regular magistrates; libationers governed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 民、夷便樂之，流移寄在其地者，不敢不奉其道。

translations.literal: The people and the barbarians found it agreeable; those who had drifted in and taken refuge in his territory did not dare fail to follow his Way.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chinese and tribal peoples alike were content under his rule, and refugees who settled in his domain dared not defy his teachings.

sentences.zh: 後遂襲取巴郡，朝廷力不能征，遂就寵魯為鎮民中郎將，領漢寧太守，通貢獻而已。

translations.literal: Later he seized Ba Commandery; the court lacked the strength to subdue him and therefore enfeoffed Zhang Lu as Pacifier of the People Central Gentleman, with him holding the post of grand administrator of Hanning, receiving only tribute in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: He later seized Ba Commandery. The court could not subdue him and therefore recognized Zhang Lu as Pacifier of the People Central Gentleman and grand administrator of Hanning, accepting only his tribute.

sentences.zh: 民有地中得玉印者，群下欲尊魯為漢寧王。

translations.literal: When a man among the people obtained a jade seal from underground, his subordinates wished to honor Zhang Lu as King of Hanning.
translations.idiomatic: When someone unearthed a jade seal, his followers wished to proclaim Zhang Lu King of Hanning.

sentences.zh: 功曹巴西閻圃諫曰：「漢川之民，戶出十萬，財富土沃，四面險固。

translations.literal: The merit officer Yan Pu of Baxi remonstrated, saying: "The people of Han River commandery number a hundred thousand households; their wealth is great and the soil fertile, and on all four sides the terrain is steep and secure.
translations.idiomatic: The merit officer Yan Pu of Baxi remonstrated: "The Han River region holds a hundred thousand households, rich soil, and natural defenses on every side.

sentences.zh: 上匡天子，則為桓、文，次及竇融，不失富貴。

translations.literal: If above you support the Son of Heaven, you will be like Duke Huan and Duke Wen; next best, like Dou Rong, you will not lose wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Support the Son of Heaven and you may become another Duke Huan or Duke Wen; at the least, follow Dou Rong's example and keep your wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 今承製署置，勢足斬斷，不煩於王。

translations.literal: Now you hold an appointment conferred by imperial writ; your power is sufficient to cut off and decide — there is no need for kingship.
translations.idiomatic: You already hold an imperial appointment with full authority — there is no need to take a royal title.

sentences.zh: 願且不稱，勿為禍先。

translations.literal: I beg that for the time being you not take the title — do not be the first to invite disaster."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you not to take the title yet — do not invite disaster first."

sentences.zh: 」魯從之。

translations.literal: " Zhang Lu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Lu took his advice.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹操軍譙，遂至浚儀，治睢陽渠。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao encamped at Qiao, then proceeded to Junyi and repaired the Suiyang canal.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao marched from Qiao to Junyi and repaired the Suiyang canal.

sentences.zh: 遣使以太牢祀橋玄。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to sacrifice to Qiao Xuan with the great offering of an ox, a sheep, and a pig.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to offer the grand sacrifice to Qiao Xuan.

sentences.zh: 進軍官渡。

translations.literal: He advanced his army to Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Guandu.

sentences.zh: 袁紹自軍敗，慚憤，發病嘔血；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao, since his army's defeat, had been ashamed and resentful; he fell ill and vomited blood;
translations.idiomatic: Since his defeat, Yuan Shao had brooded in shame and anger until he fell ill and began coughing blood;

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，薨。

translations.literal: in summer, in the fifth month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: in summer, in the fifth month, he died.

sentences.zh: 初，紹有三子：譚、熙、尚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Shao had three sons: Tan, Xi, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had three sons: Tan, Xi, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 紹後妻劉氏愛尚，數稱於紹。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao's later wife, the Lady Liu, loved Shang and repeatedly praised him to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: His second wife, Lady Liu, favored Shang and spoke of him often to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹欲以為後，而未顯言之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao wished to make him heir but had not spoken of it openly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao wished to name him heir but had never said so openly.

sentences.zh: 乃以譚繼兄後，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: He therefore had Tan succeed to his elder brother's line and sent him out as inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tan adopted into his elder brother's line and sent him out as inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 沮授諫曰：「世稱萬人逐兔，一人獲之，貪者悉止，分定故也。

translations.literal: Ju Shou remonstrated, saying: "The world says that when ten thousand men chase a rabbit and one man catches it, the greedy all stop — because the allotment is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou remonstrated: "The proverb says ten thousand men chase a rabbit, but once one man catches it the rest stop — because the prize is settled.

sentences.zh: 譚長子，當為嗣，而斥使居外，禍其始此矣。

translations.literal: Tan is the eldest son and ought to be the heir, yet you drive him to live abroad — disaster begins here."
translations.idiomatic: Tan is the eldest and should be your heir, yet you banish him abroad — your troubles begin here."

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「吾欲令諸子各據一州，以視其能。

translations.literal: " Yuan Shao said: "I wish to have each of my sons hold a province apiece, so as to observe their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shao replied, "I want each of my sons to hold a province so I can test their abilities.

sentences.zh: 」於是以中子熙為幽州刺史，外甥高幹為并州刺史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made his middle son Xi inspector of You Province and his nephew Gao Gan inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed his middle son Xi inspector of You Province and his nephew Gao Gan inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 逄紀、審配素為譚所疾，辛評、郭圖皆附於譚，而與配、紀有隙。

translations.literal: Pang Ji and Shen Pei had long been disliked by Tan; Xin Ping and Guo Tu were both attached to Tan but had rifts with Pei and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji and Shen Pei had long been at odds with Tan; Xin Ping and Guo Tu sided with Tan but feuded with Pei and Ji.

sentences.zh: 及紹薨，眾以譚長，欲立之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao died, the multitude, considering Tan the eldest, wished to install him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao died, his followers, considering Tan the eldest son, wished to make him successor.

sentences.zh: 配等恐譚立而評等為害，遂矯紹遺命，奉尚為嗣。

translations.literal: Pei and the others feared that if Tan were installed, Ping and the others would be harmed; they therefore forged Yuan Shao's final command and installed Shang as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and his faction feared that if Tan succeeded, Xin Ping and his allies would be destroyed. They forged Yuan Shao's deathbed command and installed Shang as heir.

sentences.zh: 譚至，不得立，自稱車騎將軍，屯黎陽。

translations.literal: Tan arrived but could not be installed; he styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry and garrisoned at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan arrived but was denied the succession. He styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry and encamped at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 尚少與之兵，而使逄紀隨之。

translations.literal: Shang gave him few troops and sent Pang Ji to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang gave him only a small force and sent Pang Ji to watch him.

sentences.zh: 譚求益兵，審配等又議不與。

translations.literal: Tan asked for more troops; Shen Pei and the others again deliberated and refused to give them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan asked for reinforcements, but Shen Pei and his faction again refused.

sentences.zh: 譚怒，殺逄紀。

translations.literal: Tan was angry and killed Pang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Tan flew into a rage and killed Pang Ji.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，曹操渡河攻譚。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the ninth month, Cao Cao crossed the river and attacked Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, Cao Cao crossed the Yellow River and attacked Tan.

sentences.zh: 譚告急於尚，尚留審配守鄴，自將助譚，與操相拒。

translations.literal: Tan reported the emergency to Shang; Shang left Shen Pei to guard Ye and personally led troops to aid Tan, opposing Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Tan appealed to Shang for help. Shang left Shen Pei to defend Ye and marched in person to aid Tan against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 連戰，譚、尚數敗，退而固守。

translations.literal: After repeated battles, Tan and Shang were defeated several times and withdrew to stand on the defensive.
translations.idiomatic: After several engagements Tan and Shang were repeatedly defeated and fell back to defensive positions.

sentences.zh: 尚遣所置河東太守郭援，與高幹、匈奴南單于共攻河東，發使與關中諸將馬騰等連兵，騰等陰許之，援所經城邑皆下。

translations.literal: Shang sent his appointed grand administrator of Hedong, Guo Yuan, together with Gao Gan and the Southern Chanyu of the Xiongnu to attack Hedong jointly; he dispatched envoys to link arms with the generals of Guanzhong such as Ma Teng, and Teng and the others secretly agreed; every city and town that Guo Yuan passed submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shang sent his appointee Guo Yuan, grand administrator of Hedong, with Gao Gan and the Southern Chanyu of the Xiongnu to attack Hedong. He sent envoys to ally with the Guanzhong generals including Ma Teng, who secretly agreed. Every city Guo Yuan passed submitted.

sentences.zh: 河東郡吏賈逵守絳，援攻之急；

translations.literal: The commandery clerk of Hedong, Jia Kui, defended Jiang; Guo Yuan pressed the attack fiercely;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui, a commandery officer of Hedong, held Jiang. Guo Yuan pressed the siege fiercely;

sentences.zh: 城將潰，父老與援約，不害逵乃降，援許之。

translations.literal: the city was about to fall; the elders made a pact with Guo Yuan that they would surrender if Jia Kui were not harmed, and Guo Yuan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: as the walls were about to give way, the elders bargained with Guo Yuan to surrender on condition that Jia Kui not be harmed. Guo Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 援欲使逵為將，以兵劫之，逵不動。

translations.literal: Guo Yuan wished to make Jia Kui a general and used armed men to coerce him, but Jia Kui did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan tried to force Jia Kui into his service at sword point, but Jia Kui would not budge.

sentences.zh: 左右引逵使叩頭，逵叱之曰：「安有國家長吏為賊叩頭！

translations.literal: His attendants pulled Jia Kui to make him kowtow; Jia Kui rebuked them, saying: "How could there be a chief official of the state kowtowing to a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants tried to force him to kowtow. Jia Kui shouted, "How can an officer of the state kowtow to a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」援怒，將斬之，或伏其上以救之。

translations.literal: " Guo Yuan was angry and was about to behead him; someone threw himself on top of Jia Kui to save him.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Yuan was furious and was about to execute him when someone threw himself over Jia Kui to shield him.

sentences.zh: 絳吏民聞將殺逵，皆乘城呼曰：「負約殺我賢君，寧俱死耳！

translations.literal: The officials and people of Jiang, hearing that Jia Kui was to be killed, all mounted the walls and shouted: "You break your pact and kill our worthy lord — we would rather all die together!"
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Jiang heard that Jia Kui was to be killed, they mounted the walls and cried, "You break your word and kill our worthy magistrate — we would rather die with him!"

sentences.zh: 」乃困於壺關，著土窖中，蓋以車輪。

translations.literal: " He was then confined at Huguan, placed in an earthen cellar, and covered with a cart wheel.
translations.idiomatic: " He was imprisoned at Huguan in an earthen pit and covered with a cart wheel.

sentences.zh: 逵謂守者曰：「此間無健兒邪，而使義士死此中乎？

translations.literal: Jia Kui said to his guards: "Are there no stalwart men here, that a man of righteousness should be left to die in this place?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui said to his guards, "Are there no brave men here, that a man of honor must die in this hole?"

sentences.zh: 」有祝公道者，適聞其言，乃夜往，盜引出逵，折械遣去，不語其姓名。

translations.literal: " There was a Zhu Gongdao who happened to hear these words; that night he went, stole Jia Kui out, broke his fetters and sent him away, and did not speak his own name.
translations.idiomatic: " A man named Zhu Gongdao happened to overhear. That night he stole in, freed Jia Kui, broke his bonds, and sent him away without revealing his name.

sentences.zh: 曹操使司隸校尉鐘繇圍南單于於平陽，未拔而援至。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent the Director of the Imperial Clan Zhong Yao to besiege the Southern Chanyu at Pingyang; the city was not yet taken when Guo Yuan arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Director of the Imperial Clan Zhong Yao to besiege the Southern Chanyu at Pingyang. The city had not fallen when Guo Yuan arrived.

sentences.zh: 繇使新豐令馮翊張既說馬騰，為言利害。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao sent the magistrate of Xinfeng, Zhang Ji of Fufeng, to persuade Ma Teng, setting forth advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao sent Zhang Ji, magistrate of Xinfeng in Fufeng, to persuade Ma Teng by explaining the stakes.

sentences.zh: 騰疑未決。

translations.literal: Ma Teng hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 傅幹說騰曰：「古人有言『順道者昌，逆德者亡』，曹公奉天子誅暴亂，法明政治，上下用命，可謂順道矣。

translations.literal: Fu Gan urged Ma Teng, saying: "The ancients had a saying, 'Those who follow the Way flourish; those who oppose virtue perish.' Lord Cao supports the Son of Heaven in punishing violence and disorder; his laws are clear and his government enlightened; superiors and subordinates obey his commands — this may be called following the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan urged Ma Teng: "The ancients said, 'Those who follow the Way prosper; those who defy virtue perish.' Lord Cao serves the Son of Heaven in punishing rebellion. His laws are clear, his government sound, and all obey — that is following the Way.

sentences.zh: 袁氏恃其強大，背棄王命，驅胡虜以陵中國，可謂逆德矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan relied on its strength, turned its back on the royal command, and drove the barbarians to oppress the Central States — this may be called opposing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan trusted in its power, defied the throne, and used barbarians to ravage the heartland — that is defying virtue.

sentences.zh: 今將軍既事有道，不盡其力，陰懷兩端，欲以坐觀成敗；

translations.literal: Now, General, you have already attached yourself to the side that follows the Way, yet you do not exert your full strength; you secretly harbor two minds and wish to sit and watch how success and failure turn out;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, General, having already sided with the righteous cause, hold back your full strength, secretly keeping two minds and waiting to see who wins;

sentences.zh: 吾恐成敗既定，奉辭責罪，將軍先為誅首矣！

translations.literal: I fear that once success and failure are settled, when he presents charges of guilt, the General will be the first to be put to death!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once the outcome is decided, Lord Cao will call you to account — and you will be the first head to fall!"

sentences.zh: 」於是騰懼。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ma Teng was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Teng was frightened.

sentences.zh: 幹因曰：「智者轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Fu Gan then said: "The wise turn misfortune into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan went on: "The wise turn disaster into opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今曹公與袁氏相持，而高幹、郭援合攻河東。

translations.literal: Now Lord Cao and the Yuan clan are locked in stalemate, while Gao Gan and Guo Yuan jointly attack Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao is locked in struggle with the Yuan clan while Gao Gan and Guo Yuan attack Hedong together.

sentences.zh: 曹公雖有萬全之計，不能禁河東之不危也。

translations.literal: Though Lord Cao has plans that are ten thousand times secure, he cannot prevent Hedong from falling into danger.
translations.idiomatic: However perfect Lord Cao's plans, he cannot keep Hedong from danger.

sentences.zh: 將軍誠能引兵討援，內外擊之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: If the General can truly lead troops to attack Guo Yuan and strike him from within and without, the enterprise is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly lead your forces against Guo Yuan and strike him from both sides, he is sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 是將軍一舉，斷袁氏之臂，解一方之急，曹公必重德將軍，將軍功名無與比矣。

translations.literal: With this one move the General would sever the Yuan clan's arm, relieve a region's urgent peril, and Lord Cao is sure to reward the General heavily — the General's fame and achievement would have no equal."
translations.idiomatic: With one stroke you would cut off the Yuan clan's arm, save a whole region, and Lord Cao would reward you richly. Your fame would have no equal."

sentences.zh: 」騰乃遣子超將兵萬餘人與繇會。

translations.literal: " Ma Teng thereupon sent his son Chao to lead more than ten thousand troops to join Zhong Yao.
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Teng sent his son Chao with more than ten thousand men to join Zhong Yao.

sentences.zh: 初，諸將以郭援眾盛，欲釋平陽去。

translations.literal: Earlier, the generals all considered Guo Yuan's forces numerous and wished to abandon Pingyang and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the generals, seeing Guo Yuan's great numbers, had wanted to abandon the siege of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 鐘繇曰：「袁氏方強，援之來，關中陰與之通，所以未悉叛者，顧吾威名故耳。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao said: "The Yuan clan is still strong; Guo Yuan has come, and Guanzhong is secretly in communication with him. The reason they have not all rebelled is simply that they look to our prestige and fame."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao said, "The Yuan clan is still powerful. Guo Yuan has come, and Guanzhong is secretly in league with him. The only reason they have not all risen is respect for our reputation."

sentences.zh: 若棄而去，示之以弱，所在之民，誰非寇仇？

translations.literal: If we abandon the siege and leave, showing them our weakness, among the people wherever we go, who would not be our enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If we withdraw and show weakness, every man in the land will become our enemy.

sentences.zh: 縱吾欲歸，其得至乎？

translations.literal: Even if we wished to return home, could we get there?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we wanted to go home, could we reach it safely?

sentences.zh: 此為未戰先自敗也。

translations.literal: This would be defeating ourselves before we have even fought.
translations.idiomatic: That would be defeat before battle.

sentences.zh: 且援剛愎好勝，必易吾軍，若渡汾為營，及其未濟擊之，可大克也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Guo Yuan is obstinate and loves to win; he is sure to underestimate our army. If he crosses the Fen to make camp, strike him before he has finished crossing and we can win a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan is arrogant and overconfident — he will underestimate us. If he crosses the Fen to make camp, strike while he is still crossing and we can crush him.

sentences.zh: 」援至，果徑前渡汾，眾止之，不從。

translations.literal: " When Guo Yuan arrived, he indeed went straight forward to cross the Fen; the multitude tried to stop him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Yuan arrived and marched straight to cross the Fen. His officers tried to stop him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 濟水未半，繇擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Before the crossing was half complete, Zhong Yao attacked and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Before half his force had crossed, Zhong Yao attacked and routed him.

sentences.zh: 戰罷，眾人皆言援死而不得其首。

translations.literal: When the battle ended, everyone said Guo Yuan was dead but his head could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle everyone said Guo Yuan was dead, but his head could not be found.

sentences.zh: 援，繇之甥也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuan was Zhong Yao's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan was Zhong Yao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 晚後，馬超校尉南安龐德，於鞬中出一頭，繇見之而哭。

translations.literal: Later, Ma Chao's commandant Pang De of Nan'an produced a head from his quiver; when Zhong Yao saw it, he wept.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Chao's commandant Pang De of Nan'an produced a head from his saddlebag. Zhong Yao saw it and wept.

sentences.zh: 德謝繇，繇曰：「援雖我甥，乃國賊也，卿何謝之有！

translations.literal: Pang De apologized to Zhong Yao; Zhong Yao said: "Though Yuan was my nephew, he was a traitor to the state — what is there for you to apologize for!"
translations.idiomatic: Pang De apologized. Zhong Yao said, "Yuan was my nephew, but he was a traitor to the state — you owe me no apology!"

sentences.zh: 」南單于遂降。

translations.literal: " The Southern Chanyu thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " The Southern Chanyu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 劉表使劉備北侵，至葉，曹操遣夏侯惇、于禁等拒之。

translations.literal: Liu Biao sent Liu Bei to invade northward as far as Ye; Cao Cao dispatched Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin, and others to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent Liu Bei north as far as Ye. Cao Cao sent Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin, and others to block him.

sentences.zh: 備一旦燒屯去，惇等追之。

translations.literal: Liu Bei suddenly burned his camp and withdrew; Dun and the others pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei suddenly burned his camp and withdrew. Xiahou Dun and the others gave chase.

sentences.zh: 裨將軍巨鹿李典曰：「賊無故退，疑必有伏。

translations.literal: Lieutenant General Li Dian of Julu said: "The bandits withdrew for no reason — I suspect there must be an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant General Li Dian of Julu said, "The enemy retreated for no reason — there must be an ambush.

sentences.zh: 南道窄狹，草木深，不可追也。

translations.literal: The southern road is narrow and confined, with deep grass and trees — we must not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: The southern road is narrow and overgrown — we must not pursue."

sentences.zh: 」惇等不聽，使典留守而追之，果入伏裡，兵大敗。

translations.literal: " Dun and the others would not listen; they left Dian to hold the rear and pursued, and indeed fell into an ambush — the army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " They would not listen, left Li Dian behind, and pursued — straight into an ambush. The army was routed.

sentences.zh: 典往救之，備乃退。

translations.literal: Dian went to rescue them, and Liu Bei then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dian rode to the rescue, and Liu Bei withdrew.

sentences.zh: 曹操下書責孫權任子，權召群僚會議，張昭、秦松等猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent a letter reproaching Sun Quan for not sending a hostage son; Sun Quan summoned his officials to council, but Zhang Zhao, Qin Song, and others hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent a letter demanding that Sun Quan send a son as hostage. Sun Quan called his officials to council, but Zhang Zhao, Qin Song, and others could not agree.

sentences.zh: 權引周瑜詣吳夫人前定議，瑜曰：「昔楚國初封，不滿百里之地。

translations.literal: Sun Quan brought Zhou Yu before Lady Wu to settle the matter; Zhou Yu said: "In former times when the state of Chu was first enfeoffed, its territory was less than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan brought Zhou Yu before Lady Wu to decide. Zhou Yu said, "When Chu was first enfeoffed, its territory was less than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 繼嗣賢能，廣土開境，遂據荊、揚，至於南海，傳業延祚，九百餘年。

translations.literal: Successive heirs were worthy and able; they broadened their territory and opened their borders, until they held Jing and Yang as far as the Southern Sea; their enterprise was handed down and their mandate extended for more than nine hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy successors expanded its borders until it held Jing and Yang to the Southern Sea, and the line endured more than nine hundred years.

sentences.zh: 今將軍承父兄餘資，兼六郡之眾，兵精糧多，將士用命，鑄山為銅，煮海為鹽，境內富饒，人不思亂，有何逼迫而欲送質！

translations.literal: Now the General inherits the surplus resources of father and elder brother, commands the multitudes of six commanderies, has elite troops and abundant grain, and officers and soldiers who obey his orders; you cast mountains into copper and boil the sea for salt — within your borders wealth abounds and the people do not think of disorder. What compulsion drives you to wish to send a hostage!
translations.idiomatic: You inherit your father and brother's legacy, command six commanderies, have elite troops and abundant grain, loyal officers and soldiers, copper from the mountains and salt from the sea — your realm is rich and your people content. What compulsion drives you to send a hostage!

sentences.zh: 質一入，不得不與曹氏相首尾，與相首尾，則命召不得不往，如此，便見制於人也。

translations.literal: Once a hostage is sent, you cannot but link head and tail with the Cao clan; once linked head and tail, when summons come you cannot but go — thus you will be controlled by another.
translations.idiomatic: Once a hostage is sent, you cannot but dance to Cao Cao's tune; when he summons you, you must obey — and you will be his puppet.

sentences.zh: 極不過一侯印，僕從十餘人，車數乘，馬數匹，豈與南面稱孤同哉！

translations.literal: At most you would receive a marquis's seal, a dozen or so attendants, a few carriages, and a few horses — how could that compare with facing south and styling yourself a lone ruler!
translations.idiomatic: At best you would receive a marquis's seal, a dozen attendants, a few carriages and horses — how could that compare with ruling as a sovereign in your own right!

sentences.zh: 不如勿遣，徐觀其變。

translations.literal: Better not to send one; watch how matters change in due time.
translations.idiomatic: Better not to send one — wait and watch how events unfold.

sentences.zh: 若曹氏能率義以正天下，將軍事之未晚；

translations.literal: If the Cao clan can lead with righteousness and set the realm right, it is not too late for the General to serve them;
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Cao can lead with righteousness and pacify the realm, it will not be too late to submit;

sentences.zh: 若圖為暴亂，彼自亡之不暇，焉能害人！

translations.literal: if he plots violence and disorder, he will be too busy destroying himself — how could he harm others!"
translations.idiomatic: if he plots violence and disorder, he will be too busy destroying himself to harm you!"

sentences.zh: 」吳夫人曰：「公瑾議是也。

translations.literal: " Lady Wu said: "Gongjin's plan is correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Wu said, "Gongjin is right.

sentences.zh: 公瑾與伯符同年，小一月耳，我視之如子也，汝其兄事之。

translations.literal: Gongjin was born in the same year as Bofu, only one month younger; I regard him as a son — you should treat him as an elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin was born in the same year as Bofu, only a month younger. I regard him as a son — treat him as your elder brother."

sentences.zh: 」遂不送質。

translations.literal: " They thereupon did not send a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: " No hostage was sent.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，曹操攻黎陽，與袁譚、袁尚戰於城下，譚、尚敗走，還鄴。

translations.literal: In spring, in the second month, Cao Cao attacked Liyang and fought Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang below the walls; Tan and Shang were defeated and fled, returning to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, Cao Cao attacked Liyang and fought Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang below the walls. Defeated, they fled back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，操追至鄴，收其麥。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao pursued to Ye and harvested their wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao pursued to Ye and reaped their wheat.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲乘勝遂攻之，郭嘉曰：「袁紹愛此二子，莫適立也。

translations.literal: The generals wished to press the victory and attack at once; Guo Jia said: "Yuan Shao loved these two sons and could not decide which to install.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to press the attack. Guo Jia said, "Yuan Shao loved both sons equally and could not choose an heir.

sentences.zh: 今權力相侔，各有黨與，急之則相保，緩之則爭心生。

translations.literal: Now their power is equal, each has his faction; press them hard and they will protect one another; relax pressure and the spirit of rivalry will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Now their power is equal and each has his faction. Press them and they will unite; relax pressure and rivalry will break out.

sentences.zh: 不如南向荊州以待其變，變成而後擊之，可一舉定也。

translations.literal: Better to turn south toward Jing Province and await their change; when the change is complete, then strike — the realm can be settled in one move."
translations.idiomatic: Better march south toward Jing Province and wait for them to turn on each other. Strike when they split — and you can settle the north in one blow."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」五月，操還許，留其將賈信屯黎陽。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, Cao Cao returned to Xu and left his general Jia Xin to garrison at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month he returned to Xu and left Jia Xin to garrison Liyang.

sentences.zh: 譚謂尚曰：「我鎧甲不精，故前為曹操所敗。

translations.literal: Tan said to Shang: "My armor was not fine, and that is why I was defeated by Cao Cao before.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said to Shang, "My armor was poor — that is why Cao Cao defeated us.

sentences.zh: 今操軍退，人懷歸志，及其未濟，出兵掩之，可令大潰，此策不可失也。

translations.literal: Now Cao Cao's army has withdrawn and his men long to return home; before they have finished crossing the river, send troops to strike them in ambush — you can make them collapse utterly. This plan must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Now Cao Cao is withdrawing and his men long for home. Strike before they finish crossing the river and you can rout them utterly. This chance must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 」尚疑之，既不益兵，又不易甲。

translations.literal: " Shang was suspicious; he neither increased the troops nor replaced the armor.
translations.idiomatic: " Shang was suspicious and neither sent reinforcements nor replaced the armor.

sentences.zh: 譚大怒，郭圖、辛評因謂譚曰：「使先公出將軍為兄後者，皆審配之謀也。

translations.literal: Tan was greatly angry; Guo Tu and Xin Ping thereupon said to Tan: "It was all Shen Pei's plotting that made your late father send the General out as successor to your elder brother's line."
translations.idiomatic: Tan was furious. Guo Tu and Xin Ping said, "It was Shen Pei who persuaded your father to send you out as heir to your elder brother's line."

sentences.zh: 」譚遂引兵攻尚，戰於門外。

translations.literal: " Tan thereupon led troops to attack Shang and fought outside the gates.
translations.idiomatic: " Tan marched against Shang and fought outside the gates.

sentences.zh: 譚敗，引兵還南皮。

translations.literal: Tan was defeated and led his troops back to Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was defeated and withdrew to Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 別駕北海王修率吏民自青州往救譚。

translations.literal: The chief aide Wang Xiu of Beihai led officials and people from Qing Province to go rescue Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Chief aide Wang Xiu of Beihai led officials and people from Qing Province to rescue Tan.

sentences.zh: 譚欲更還攻尚，修曰：「兄弟者，左右手也。

translations.literal: Tan wished to return and attack Shang again; Wang Xiu said: "Brothers are like the left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Tan wanted to attack Shang again. Wang Xiu said, "Brothers are like left and right hands.

sentences.zh: 譬人將鬥而斷其右手，曰『我必勝』，其可乎？

translations.literal: It is as if a man about to fight were to cut off his right hand and say, 'I am sure to win' — could that be done?
translations.idiomatic: It is as if a man about to fight cut off his right hand and said, 'I am sure to win' — could that work?

sentences.zh: 夫棄兄弟而不親，天下其誰親之！

translations.literal: If you cast aside your brother and do not draw close to him, who in the world will draw close to you!
translations.idiomatic: Cast aside your brother and who in the world will stand with you!

sentences.zh: 彼讒人離間骨肉以求一朝之利，願塞耳勿聽也。

translations.literal: Those slanderers sunder flesh and bone for a moment's profit — I beg you stop your ears and do not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers sunder flesh and blood for momentary gain — stop your ears and do not listen to them.

sentences.zh: 若斬佞臣數人，復相親睦，以御四方，可橫行於天下。

translations.literal: If you behead a few flatterers and become close and harmonious again, using that strength to face the four quarters, you can march at will through the world."
translations.idiomatic: Behead a few flatterers, reconcile with your brother, and face the four quarters together — then you can march at will through the world."

sentences.zh: 」譚不從。

translations.literal: " Tan would not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Tan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 譚將劉詢起兵漯陰以叛譚，諸城皆應之。

translations.literal: Tan's general Liu Xun raised troops at Luoyin to rebel against Tan, and all the cities responded.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's general Liu Xun rebelled at Luoyin, and cities throughout the province rose with him.

sentences.zh: 譚歎曰：「今舉州皆叛，豈孤之不德邪？

translations.literal: Tan sighed and said: "Now the whole province rebels — is it because of my lack of virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Tan sighed, "The whole province rebels — have I so little virtue as this?"

sentences.zh: 」王修曰：「東萊太守管統，雖在海表，此人不反，必來。

translations.literal: " Wang Xiu said: "Guan Tong, grand administrator of Donglai — though he is beyond the sea, this man will not rebel; he is sure to come."
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xiu said, "Guan Tong, grand administrator of Donglai — though he is far across the sea, he will not rebel. He is sure to come."

sentences.zh: 」後十餘日，統果棄其妻子來赴譚，妻子為賊所殺。

translations.literal: " More than ten days later, Guan Tong indeed abandoned his wife and children to come to Tan; his wife and children were killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later Guan Tong abandoned his wife and children to join Tan. Bandits killed his family on the way.

sentences.zh: 譚更以統為樂安太守。

translations.literal: Tan again appointed Guan Tong grand administrator of Lean.
translations.idiomatic: Tan appointed Guan Tong grand administrator of Lean.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，操擊劉表，軍於西平。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, Cao Cao attacked Liu Biao and encamped at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Cao Cao attacked Liu Biao and encamped at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 袁尚自將攻袁譚，大破之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shang personally led troops to attack Yuan Tan and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang personally attacked Yuan Tan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 譚奔平原，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Tan fled to Pingyuan and, relying on the city walls, held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Tan fled to Pingyuan and held the city against siege.

sentences.zh: 尚圍之急，譚遣辛評弟毘詣曹操請救。

translations.literal: As Shang pressed the siege urgently, Tan sent Xin Ping's younger brother Pi to Cao Cao to beg for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, Tan sent Xin Ping's brother Pi to Cao Cao to beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 劉表以書諫譚曰：「君子違難不適仇國，交絕不出惡聲，況忘先人之仇，棄親戚之好，而為萬世之戒，遺同盟之恥哉！

translations.literal: Liu Biao sent a letter admonishing Tan, saying: "A gentleman fleeing hardship does not go to an enemy state; when relations are severed he does not utter harsh words — how much less forget his father's enmity and cast aside kinship, making himself a warning for ten thousand generations and leaving shame upon his allies!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao wrote to admonish Tan: "A gentleman in distress does not flee to an enemy state; when ties are broken he does not speak harshly — how much less forget his father's enemy, abandon his kin, become a warning to posterity, and shame his allies!"

sentences.zh: 若冀州有不弟之傲，仁君當降志辱身，以濟事為務，事定之後，使天下平其曲直，不亦為高義邪？

translations.literal: If in Ji Province there is a younger brother's arrogance, the benevolent lord ought to lower his will and humble his person, making success of the enterprise his task; when the affair is settled, let the realm judge right and wrong — would that not also be lofty righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: If your brother in Ji Province is arrogant, you should humble yourself for the greater cause. When matters are settled, let the world judge who was right — would that not be the noble course?"

sentences.zh: 」又與尚書曰：「金、木、水、火以剛柔相濟，然後克得其和，能為民用。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to Shang, saying: "Metal, wood, water, and fire complement one another through hardness and softness; only then can harmony be attained and they serve the people's use.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote to Shang: "Metal, wood, water, and fire balance hardness and softness to achieve harmony and serve the people's needs.

sentences.zh: 今青州天性峭急，迷於曲直。

translations.literal: Now Qing Province by nature is precipitous and hasty, confused about right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Province is by nature harsh and hasty, blind to right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 仁君度數弘廣，綽然有餘，當以大包小，以優容劣，先除曹操以卒先公之恨，事定之後，乃議曲直之計，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: The benevolent lord's measure is broad and ample, with room to spare; you ought to use the large to embrace the small and the superior to tolerate the inferior — first eliminate Cao Cao to fulfill your late father's hatred; after the affair is settled, then discuss the plan for right and wrong — would that not also be good!"
translations.idiomatic: You, my lord, are magnanimous and have room to spare. Embrace the smaller, tolerate the weaker — first destroy Cao Cao to avenge your father. Settle that, then judge right and wrong between you — would that not be wise!"

sentences.zh: 若迷而不反，則胡夷將有譏誚之言，況我同盟，復能戮力為君之役哉？

translations.literal: If you are lost and do not turn back, then the barbarians will have words of mockery — how much less can we allies exert our strength in your service?
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in error, even barbarians will mock you — how can your allies fight for you?

sentences.zh: 此韓盧、東郭自困於前面遺田父之獲者也。

translations.literal: This is like the hound Han Lu and the hare Dongguo exhausting themselves in front and leaving the catch to the field farmer."
translations.idiomatic: This is the hound and hare exhausting each other while the farmer reaps the prize."

sentences.zh: 」譚、尚皆不從。

translations.literal: " Tan and Shang both would not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Neither Tan nor Shang listened.

sentences.zh: 辛毘至西平見曹操，致譚意，群下多以為劉表強，宜先平之，譚、尚不足憂也。

translations.literal: Xin Pi came to Xiping to see Cao Cao and conveyed Tan's intent; the subordinates mostly thought Liu Biao was strong and that he ought to be pacified first — Tan and Shang were not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi came to Xiping and conveyed Tan's plea. Most of Cao Cao's advisers thought Liu Biao was the real threat and Tan and Shang could wait.

sentences.zh: 荀攸曰：「天下方有事，而劉表坐保江、漢之間，其無四方之志可知矣。

translations.literal: Xun You said: "The realm is still in turmoil, yet Liu Biao sits guarding the lands between the Yangtze and Han — it is plain that he has no ambition for the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "The realm is still in turmoil, yet Liu Biao merely holds the Yangtze and Han — he clearly has no ambition beyond his own domain.

sentences.zh: 袁氏據四州之地，帶甲數十萬，紹以寬厚得眾心；

translations.literal: The Yuan clan held the territory of four provinces and fielded several hundred thousand armored men; Yuan Shao won the people's hearts through generosity;
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan held four provinces and fielded hundreds of thousands of men. Yuan Shao won hearts through generosity.

sentences.zh: 使二子和睦以守其成業，則天下之難未息也。

translations.literal: if the two sons were harmonious in guarding their established enterprise, the realm's troubles would not cease.
translations.idiomatic: If his two sons united to hold his legacy, the realm's troubles would never end.

sentences.zh: 今兄弟遘惡，其勢不兩全，若有所並則力專，力專則難圖也。

translations.literal: Now the brothers have met with enmity; their power cannot both survive. If one absorbs the other, his strength will be concentrated — and concentrated strength is hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Now the brothers are at war and cannot both survive. When one absorbs the other, his power will be concentrated — and concentrated power is hard to overcome.

sentences.zh: 及其亂而取之，天下定矣，此時不可失也。

translations.literal: Take them while they are in disorder and the realm will be settled — this moment must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they are in chaos and the realm is yours — this moment must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 」操從之。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 後數日，操更欲先平荊州，使譚、尚自相敝，辛毘望操色，知有變，以語郭嘉。

translations.literal: Several days later, Cao Cao again wished to pacify Jing Province first and let Tan and Shang wear each other down; Xin Pi watched Cao Cao's expression, knew there had been a change, and told Guo Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Cao Cao again favored attacking Jing Province first and letting the Yuan brothers destroy each other. Xin Pi read his face, sensed the change, and told Guo Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰操，操謂毘曰：「譚必可信，尚必可克不？

translations.literal: Guo Jia spoke to Cao Cao, and Cao Cao said to Pi: "Is Tan surely trustworthy? Is Shang surely conquerable?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia spoke to Cao Cao, who then asked Pi, "Can Tan be trusted? Can Shang be conquered?"

sentences.zh: 」毘對曰：「明公無問信與詐也，直當論其勢耳。

translations.literal: " Pi replied: "My lord, do not ask about trustworthiness or deceit — you should speak only of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi replied, "My lord, do not ask about trust or deceit — speak only of the situation.

sentences.zh: 袁氏本兄弟相伐，非謂他人能間其間，乃謂天下可定於己也。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan originally fought as brothers, not thinking others could sow discord between them, but believing the realm could be settled by themselves alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan brothers fought each other believing no outsider could divide them and that they alone could rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 今一旦求救於明公，此可知也。

translations.literal: Now in a single day they beg rescue from my lord — from this it can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now they beg you for rescue in a single day — that tells you everything.

sentences.zh: 顯甫見顯思困而不能取，此力竭也。

translations.literal: Xianfu sees Xiansi in distress yet cannot take him — this is exhaustion of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Tan sees Shang in distress yet cannot defeat him — his strength is spent.

sentences.zh: 兵革敗於外，謀臣誅於內，兄弟讒鬩，國分為二，連年戰伐，介冑生蟣虱，加以旱蝗，饑饉並臻；

translations.literal: Armies are defeated abroad, strategists executed within, brothers slander and quarrel, the state is split in two, year after year of warfare until armor breeds lice, joined by drought, locusts, and famine together;
translations.idiomatic: Armies are defeated abroad, advisers executed at home, brothers feud, the state is split in two, years of war have bred lice in the armor, and drought, locusts, and famine have struck together;

sentences.zh: 天災應於上，人事困於下，民無愚智，皆知土崩瓦解，此乃天亡尚之時也。

translations.literal: heavenly disasters respond above, human affairs are distressed below — among the people, wise and foolish alike, all know the state is crumbling and disintegrating; this is the time when Heaven is destroying Shang.
translations.idiomatic: disaster strikes from above and distress from below — wise and foolish alike know the state is crumbling. Heaven itself is destroying Shang.

sentences.zh: 今往攻鄴，尚不還救，即不能自守；

translations.literal: If you now go to attack Ye, Shang will not return to rescue it and cannot hold it himself;
translations.idiomatic: Attack Ye now — Shang will not abandon the siege to rescue it and cannot hold it;

sentences.zh: 還救，即譚踵其後。

translations.literal: if he returns to rescue, Tan will follow at his heels.
translations.idiomatic: if he returns, Tan will follow at his heels.

sentences.zh: 以明公之威，應困窮之敵，擊疲敝之寇，無異迅風之振秋葉矣。

translations.literal: With my lord's prestige, meeting a cornered enemy and striking a worn-out foe — it is no different from a swift wind shaking autumn leaves.
translations.idiomatic: With your prestige against a desperate, exhausted foe — it will be like a gale shaking autumn leaves.

sentences.zh: 天以尚與明公，明公不取而伐荊州，荊州豐樂，國未有釁。

translations.literal: Heaven is giving Shang to my lord; if my lord does not take him but instead attacks Jing Province — Jing Province is rich and content, its state has no crack.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is handing Shang to you. If you pass him by to attack rich, content Jing Province — a land without a crack in its armor —

sentences.zh: 仲虺有言，『取亂侮亡』。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui had a saying: 'Take the disorderly and insult the perishing.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui said, 'Strike the disorderly and trample the perishing.'

sentences.zh: 方今二袁不務遠略而內相圖，可謂亂矣；

translations.literal: At present the two Yuans do not pursue far-reaching strategy but plot against each other within — this may be called disorder;
translations.idiomatic: The two Yuans plot against each other instead of looking outward — that is disorder;

sentences.zh: 居者無食，行者無糧，可謂亡矣。

translations.literal: those who stay have no food, those who march have no grain — this may be called perishing.
translations.idiomatic: those who stay have no food, those who march have no grain — that is ruin.

sentences.zh: 朝不謀夕，民命靡繼，而不綏之，欲待他年；

translations.literal: They do not plan beyond the morning for the evening; the people's lives cannot continue — yet you do not pacify them and wish to wait for another year;
translations.idiomatic: They cannot plan beyond today; the people's lives hang by a thread — yet you would wait;

sentences.zh: 他年或登，又自知亡而改修厥德，失所以用兵之要矣。

translations.literal: in another year one of them may prevail, then knowing he was perishing he will reform his virtue — you will have lost the essential point of using arms.
translations.idiomatic: next year one may prevail, reform his ways, and grow strong again — and you will have missed the essential moment for war.

sentences.zh: 今因其請救而撫之，利莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now, because they beg rescue, comfort them — the profit could not be greater.
translations.idiomatic: Accept their plea for aid now — the gain could not be greater.

sentences.zh: 且四方之寇，莫大於河北，河北平，則六軍盛而天下震矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the foes of the four quarters, none is greater than Hebei; when Hebei is pacified, the six armies will flourish and the realm will tremble."
translations.idiomatic: Among all foes, none is greater than Hebei. Pacify Hebei and your armies will flourish and the realm will tremble."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」乃許譚平。

translations.literal: " He thereupon agreed to make peace with Tan.
translations.idiomatic: " He agreed to aid Tan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，操至黎陽。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao reached Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao reached Liyang.

sentences.zh: 尚聞操渡河，乃釋平原還鄴。

translations.literal: When Shang heard that Cao Cao had crossed the river, he abandoned the siege of Pingyuan and returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang heard Cao Cao had crossed the river, he abandoned Pingyuan and returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尚將呂曠、高翔畔歸曹操，譚復陰刻將軍印以假曠、翔。

translations.literal: Shang's generals Lu Kuang and Gao Xiang defected to Cao Cao; Tan again secretly carved general's seals to lend to Kuang and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang's generals Lu Kuang and Gao Xiang defected to Cao Cao. Tan secretly carved general's seals to win them back.

sentences.zh: 操知譚詐，乃為子整娉譚女以安之，而引軍還。

translations.literal: Cao Cao knew Tan was deceitful; he therefore betrothed his son Zheng to Tan's daughter to reassure him, then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Tan was deceitful, Cao Cao betrothed his son Zheng to Tan's daughter to reassure him, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 孫權西伐黃祖，破其舟軍，惟城未克，而山寇復動。

translations.literal: Sun Quan attacked Huang Zu in the west, defeated his fleet, but only the city was not taken when mountain bandits stirred again.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan attacked Huang Zu in the west and destroyed his fleet, but had not taken the city when mountain bandits rose again.

sentences.zh: 權還，過豫章，使征虜中郎將呂范平鄱陽、會稽，蕩寇中郎將程普討樂安，建昌都尉太史慈領海昏，以別部司馬黃蓋、韓當、周泰、呂蒙等守劇縣令長，討山越，悉平之。

translations.literal: Sun Quan returned, passed through Yuzhang, sent the General Who Suppresses Barbarians Central Gentleman Lu Fan to pacify Poyang and Kuaiji, the General Who Sweeps Bandits Central Gentleman Cheng Pu to attack Lean, the Commandant of Jianchang Taishi Ci to hold Haihun, and with Separate Division Major Huang Gai, Han Dang, Zhou Tai, Lu Meng, and others to guard the county magistrates of Ju, suppressing the Shanyue — all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan withdrew, passed through Yuzhang, and dispatched Lu Fan to pacify Poyang and Kuaiji, Cheng Pu to attack Lean, Taishi Ci to hold Haihun, and Huang Gai, Han Dang, Zhou Tai, Lu Meng, and others to garrison the counties and suppress the Shanyue — all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 建安、漢興、南平民作亂，聚眾各萬餘人，權使南部都尉會稽賀齊進討，皆平之，復立縣邑，料出兵萬人；

translations.literal: The people of Jian'an, Hanxing, and Nanping rebelled, each gathering forces of more than ten thousand; Quan sent the Southern Commandant of Kuaiji He Qi to advance and attack — all were pacified; he reestablished counties and districts and assessed a levy of ten thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an, Hanxing, and Nanping the people rebelled, each district raising more than ten thousand men. Sun Quan sent He Qi of Kuaiji, Southern Commandant, to suppress them. All were pacified; counties were reestablished and ten thousand troops were conscripted.

sentences.zh: 拜齊平東校尉。

translations.literal: [Sun Quan] appointed Qi Colonel Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan appointed He Qi Colonel Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹操濟河，遏淇水入白溝以通糧道。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao crossed the river, dammed the Qi River into the White Ditch to open a grain-supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao crossed the Yellow River and diverted the Qi River into the White Ditch to secure his supply line.

sentences.zh: 二月，袁尚復攻袁譚於平原，留其將審配、蘇由守鄴。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yuan Shang again attacked Yuan Tan at Pingyuan, leaving his generals Shen Pei and Su You to defend Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yuan Shang resumed his attack on Yuan Tan at Pingyuan, leaving Shen Pei and Su You to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 曹操進軍至洹水，蘇由欲為內應，謀洩，出奔操。

translations.literal: Cao Cao advanced to the Huan River; Su You wished to serve as an inside collaborator, but the plot leaked and he fled to join Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched to the Huan River. Su You tried to act as an inside agent, but the plot was discovered and he fled to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操進至鄴，為土山、地道以攻之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao advanced to Ye and built ramparts and tunnels to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pushed on to Ye and built siege mounds and tunnels to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 尚武安長尹楷屯毛城，以通上黨糧道。

translations.literal: Shang's Commandant of Wu'an Yin Kai encamped at Maocheng to keep open the Shangdang grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kai, magistrate of Wu'an under Shang, held Maocheng to keep the Shangdang supply line open.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，操留曹洪攻鄴，自將擊楷，破之而還。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao left Cao Hong to attack Ye and personally led troops to strike Kai, defeated him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao left Cao Hong to besiege Ye and personally routed Yin Kai, then returned.

sentences.zh: 又擊尚將沮鵠於邯鄲，拔之。

translations.literal: He also attacked Shang's general Ju Hu at Handan and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Shang's general Ju Hu at Handan and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 易陽令韓范、涉長梁岐皆舉縣降。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Yiyang Han Fan and the chief of She Liang Qi both led their counties in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan of Yiyang and Liang Qi of She surrendered with their entire districts.

sentences.zh: 徐晃言於操曰：「二袁未破，諸城未下者傾耳而聽，宜旌賞二縣以示諸城。

translations.literal: Xu Huang said to Cao Cao: "The two Yuans are not yet broken; the cities not yet taken all listen with tilted ears — you ought to commend and reward these two counties to show the other cities."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang urged Cao Cao: "The Yuan brothers still hold out, and every city that has not surrendered is watching closely. Reward these two counties to set an example for the rest."

sentences.zh: 」操從之，范、岐皆賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao followed this advice; Fan and Qi were both enfeoffed as Marquises within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao agreed. Han Fan and Liang Qi were both enfeoffed as marquises within the passes.

sentences.zh: 黑山賊帥張燕遣使求助，操拜平北將軍。

translations.literal: The Black Mountain bandit chief Zhang Yan sent envoys begging aid; Cao Cao appointed him General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, chief of the Black Mountain bandits, sent envoys to ask for help. Cao Cao appointed him General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 五月，操毀土山、地道，鑿塹圍城，周回四十里，初令淺，示若可越。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Cao Cao destroyed the ramparts and tunnels, dug moats and encircled the city — forty li in circumference — at first making them shallow to show as if they could be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Cao Cao tore down his siege mounds and tunnels, dug a forty-li encircling moat, and at first left it shallow, as though it could be crossed easily.

sentences.zh: 配望見，笑之，不出爭利。

translations.literal: Pei saw it from afar, laughed at it, and did not come out to contest the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei looked out and laughed, and made no sortie to seize the ground.

sentences.zh: 操一夜浚之，廣深二丈，引漳水以灌之；

translations.literal: In one night Cao Cao deepened it — twenty feet wide and deep — and diverted the Zhang River to flood it;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao deepened it in a single night to twenty feet across and deep, then diverted the Zhang River to flood the moat;

sentences.zh: 城中餓死者過半。

translations.literal: Within the city more than half died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the people in the city starved to death.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，尚將兵萬餘人還救鄴；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Shang led more than ten thousand men back to rescue Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Shang marched back toward Ye with more than ten thousand men;

sentences.zh: 未到，欲令審配知外動止，先使主簿巨鹿李孚入城。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, wishing to let Shen Pei know the movements outside, he first sent Registrar Li Fu of Julu into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, he wanted Shen Pei to know what was happening outside and first sent Li Fu of Julu, his chief clerk, into the city.

sentences.zh: 孚斫問事杖，繫著馬邊，自著平上幘，將三騎，投暮詣鄴下；

translations.literal: Fu hewed an official's staff, tied it at his horse's side, put on a plain cap himself, took three horsemen, and at dusk went to Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu cut himself a staff of office, tied it to his saddle, put on a plain cap, took three riders, and reached Ye at dusk;

sentences.zh: 自稱都督，歷北圍，循表而東，步步呵責守圍將士，隨輕重行其罰。

translations.literal: Calling himself commander-in-chief, he passed through the northern encirclement, followed along the outer line eastward, step by step rebuking the encircling officers and soldiers and inflicting punishments according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to be the army inspector, walked the northern siege line eastward along the perimeter, and at every step berated the guards and punished them according to their offenses.

sentences.zh: 遂歷操營，前至南圍，當章門，復責怒守圍者，收縛之。

translations.literal: He then passed through Cao Cao's camps, going forward to the southern encirclement at Zhang Gate, again berating in anger the encircling guards and arresting and binding them.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Cao Cao's camps to the southern siege line at Zhang Gate, again upbraided the guards, and had them bound.

sentences.zh: 因開其圍，馳到城下，呼城上人，城上人以繩引，孚得入。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened their encirclement, galloped to the foot of the wall, called up to those on the wall, and those above lowered a rope and drew him in.
translations.idiomatic: He had the cordon opened, rode to the wall, called up to the defenders, and was pulled inside by rope.

sentences.zh: 配等見孚，悲喜，鼓噪稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Pei and the others, seeing Fu, were grieved and joyful, beating drums and shouting "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei and the others greeted him with mingled grief and joy, shouting and cheering for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 守圍者以狀聞，操笑曰：「此非徒得入也，方且復出。

translations.literal: The encircling guards reported the matter; Cao Cao smiled and said: "This one did not merely get in — he is about to get out again."
translations.idiomatic: When the guards reported what had happened, Cao Cao laughed and said, "He didn't come in just to stay — he'll be getting out again soon."

sentences.zh: 」孚知外圍益急，不可復冒，乃請配悉出城中老弱以省谷，夜，簡別數千人，皆使持白幡，從三門並出降。

translations.literal: " Fu knew the outer encirclement was daily tighter and that he could not again take the risk; he therefore asked Pei to send out all the old and weak in the city to save grain; at night he selected several thousand, all made to carry white banners, and from three gates together they went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Knowing he could not bluff his way through the tightening ring a second time, Li Fu persuaded Shen Pei to send out the city's elderly and weak to save grain. That night he sorted out several thousand people, gave them white banners, and sent them out through three gates at once to surrender.

sentences.zh: 孚復將三騎作降人服，隨輩夜出，突圍得去。

translations.literal: Fu again took three horsemen disguised as surrendering men, followed the throng out by night, burst through the encirclement, and got away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu then disguised himself and his three riders as refugees, slipped out with the crowd that night, and broke through the siege lines.

sentences.zh: 尚兵既至，諸將皆以為：「此歸師，人自為戰，不如避之。

translations.literal: When Shang's army had arrived, the generals all considered: "This is a returning army; each man will fight for himself — better to avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: When Shang's army arrived, his commanders argued: "These are men hurrying home to save their city. They will fight as if each man alone mattered. We ought to avoid them."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「尚從大道來，當避之；

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "If Shang comes by the great road, we ought to avoid him;
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "If Shang comes by the main road, we should avoid him;

sentences.zh: 若循西山來者，此成禽耳。

translations.literal: If he comes along the western hills, this will be catching prey."
translations.idiomatic: but if he comes by the western hills, he will be easy prey."

sentences.zh: 」尚果循西山來，東至陽平亭，去鄴十七里，臨滏水為營。

translations.literal: " Shang indeed came along the western hills, proceeding east to Yangping Pavilion, seventeen li from Ye, and encamped on the Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: " Shang did come by the western hills, reached Yangping Pavilion seventeen li from Ye, and made camp on the Fu River.

sentences.zh: 夜，舉火以示城中，城中亦舉火相應。

translations.literal: At night he raised fires to signal the city; the city also raised fires in answer.
translations.idiomatic: At night he lit signal fires for the city, and the city answered with fires of its own.

sentences.zh: 配出兵城北，欲與尚對決圍。

translations.literal: Pei led troops out from the north of the city, wishing to meet Shang and break the encirclement face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei led troops out from the north gate, intending to link up with Shang and break the siege.

sentences.zh: 操逆擊之，敗還，尚亦破走，依曲漳為營，操遂圍之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao struck them in reverse, defeated them and they retreated; Shang was also routed and fled, relying on the Qu Zhang for an encampment — Cao Cao then encircled him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao counterattacked and drove Shen Pei back. Shang was also routed and withdrew to the Qu Zhang to make camp, where Cao Cao besieged him.

sentences.zh: 未合，尚懼，遣使求降；

translations.literal: Before the encirclement closed, Shang was afraid and sent envoys to beg surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Before the ring closed, Shang, alarmed, sent envoys to sue for peace;

sentences.zh: 操不聽，圍之益急。

translations.literal: Cao Cao would not listen and pressed the encirclement the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 尚夜遁，保祁山，操復進圍之。

translations.literal: Shang fled by night, took refuge at Qishan — Cao Cao again advanced and encircled him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang fled by night to Qishan. Cao Cao pursued and besieged him again.

sentences.zh: 尚將馬延、張顗等臨陳降，眾大潰，尚奔中山。

translations.literal: Shang's generals Ma Yan, Zhang Yi, and others surrendered before the battle line; the masses greatly collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shang's generals Ma Yan and Zhang Yi surrendered on the field. His army collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 盡收其輜重，得尚印綬、節鉞及衣物，以示城中，城中崩沮。

translations.literal: [Cao Cao] took all his baggage train, obtained Shang's seal ribbon, tally and axe of authority, and clothing, and displayed them to the city — within the city spirits collapsed in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao captured all his supplies, along with Shang's seals, credentials, and regalia, and displayed them before Ye. The city's morale shattered.

sentences.zh: 審配令士卒曰：「堅守死戰！

translations.literal: Shen Pei ordered the soldiers: "Hold fast and fight to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei told the troops: "Hold the walls and fight to the death!"

sentences.zh: 操軍疲矣，幽州方至，何憂無主！

translations.literal: Cao Cao's army is exhausted; forces from You Province are just arriving — why worry that there will be no lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army is spent, and reinforcements from You Province are on the way. Why fear that we are leaderless?"

sentences.zh: 」操出行圍，配伏弩射之，幾中。

translations.literal: " When Cao Cao went out on an inspection of the encirclement, Pei hid crossbowmen who shot at him — he was nearly hit.
translations.idiomatic: " When Cao Cao rode out to inspect the siege lines, Shen Pei had crossbowmen hidden to shoot at him. The bolts nearly found their mark.

sentences.zh: 配兄子榮為東門校尉，八月，戊寅，榮夜開門內操兵。

translations.literal: Pei's elder brother's son Rong was Commandant of the East Gate; on the day wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and admitted Cao Cao's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei's nephew Rong commanded the east gate. On wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and let Cao Cao's men in.

sentences.zh: 配拒戰城中，操兵生獲之。

translations.literal: Pei resisted in battle within the city, and Cao Cao's troops took him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei fought on inside the city until Cao Cao's men captured him alive.

sentences.zh: 辛評家系鄴獄，辛毘馳往，欲解之，已悉為配所殺。

translations.literal: Xin Ping's family was imprisoned in Ye; Xin Pi galloped there wishing to release them, but they had already all been killed by Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ping's family was held in the Ye jail. Xin Pi rushed to free them, but Shen Pei had already had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 操兵縛配詣帳下，毘逆以馬鞭擊其頭，罵之曰：「奴，汝今日真死矣！

translations.literal: Cao Cao's troops bound Pei and brought him beneath the tent; Pi went up to him and struck his head with a riding crop, cursing him: "Slave — today you truly die!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's men bound Shen Pei and brought him to headquarters. Xin Pi met him and whipped him across the head, shouting, "You slave — this time you are truly dead!"

sentences.zh: 」配顧曰：「狗輩，正由汝曹破我冀州，恨不得殺汝也！

translations.literal: " Pei turned and said: "Dog pack — it was precisely you lot who ruined my Ji Province; I only regret I could not kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Pei turned and said, "You curs — it was your kind who ruined Ji Province. I only regret I could not kill you!"

sentences.zh: 且汝今日能殺生我邪？

translations.literal: And can you today kill me while I yet live?"
translations.idiomatic: And as I still live, can you kill me now?"

sentences.zh: 」有頃，操引見，謂配曰：「曩日孤之行圍，何弩之多也！

translations.literal: " After a while Cao Cao had him brought in and said to Pei: "The other day when I inspected the encirclement, how many crossbow bolts there were!"
translations.idiomatic: " After a time Cao Cao had him brought before him and said, "When I rode the lines the other day, your crossbow bolts came thick as rain."

sentences.zh: 」配曰：「猶恨其少！

translations.literal: " Pei said: "I still regret there were too few!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Pei said, "I only regret there were not more."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「卿忠於袁氏，亦自不得不爾。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "You were loyal to the Yuans — you could not have acted otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "You were loyal to the Yuan house. You could not have done otherwise."

sentences.zh: 」意欲活之。

translations.literal: " He intended to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to spare him.

sentences.zh: 配意氣壯烈，終於橈辭，而辛毘等號哭不已，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Pei's spirit and bearing were fierce and bold; to the end he would not soften his words — but Xin Pi and the others wept and wailed without cease, and so he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei remained fierce and unyielding to the end, but Xin Pi and the others kept wailing until Cao Cao ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 冀州人張子謙先降，素與配不善，笑謂配曰：「正南，卿竟何如我？

translations.literal: The Ji Province native Zhang Ziqian had surrendered earlier; he had always been on bad terms with Pei and, laughing, said to Pei: "Zhengnan — in the end how do you compare with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziqian of Ji Province, who had surrendered earlier and had never been on good terms with Shen Pei, mocked him: "Zhengnan — see how much better I fare than you?"

sentences.zh: 」配厲聲曰：「汝為降虜，審配為忠臣。

translations.literal: " Pei said in a harsh voice: "You are a surrendered captive; Shen Pei is a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Pei shouted back, "You are a turncoat. I am a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 雖死，豈羨汝生邪！

translations.literal: Though I die, why should I envy your living?"
translations.idiomatic: Even in death, why should I envy your life?"

sentences.zh: 」臨行刑，叱持兵者令北向，曰：「我君在北也。

translations.literal: " Facing execution, he shouted at those holding the weapons to make him face north, saying: "My lord is in the north."
translations.idiomatic: " At the moment of execution he ordered the executioners to turn him north, saying, "My lord is in the north."

sentences.zh: 操乃臨祀紹墓，哭之流涕；

translations.literal: Cao Cao then went in person to worship at Shao's tomb and wept with streaming tears;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao went in person to Yuan Shao's tomb and wept there;

sentences.zh: 慰勞紹妻，還其家人寶物，賜雜繒絮，稟食之。

translations.literal: He comforted Shao's wife, returned her household treasures, bestowed assorted silks and cotton padding, and provided rations for them.
translations.idiomatic: He consoled Yuan Shao's widow, restored her family's property, gave her cloth and supplies, and provided rations for her household.

sentences.zh: 初，袁紹與操共起兵，紹問操曰：「若事不輯，則方面何所可據？
