translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Shao and Cao Cao jointly raised troops, Shao asked Cao Cao: "If affairs do not succeed, on what region can one rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuan Shao and Cao Cao first raised armies together, Shao asked Cao Cao, "If things go wrong, what territory should one hold?"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「足下意以為何如？

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "What does Your Grace think?"
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao replied, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「吾南據河，北阻燕、代，兼戎狄之眾，南向以爭天下，庶可以濟乎！

translations.literal: " Shao said: "I would hold the Yellow River in the south, block Yan and Dai in the north, take the multitudes of the Rong and Di together, and turn south to contest the realm — perhaps that could succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shao said, "I would hold the Yellow River in the south, block the passes to Yan and Dai in the north, rally the northern tribes, and march south to seize the empire. That might work."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「吾任天下之智力，以道御之，無所不可。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao said: "I would employ the intelligence and strength of the realm, govern them by the Way — nothing would be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "I would gather the talents of the realm and lead them by principle. With that, anything is possible."

sentences.zh: 九月，詔以操領冀州牧；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict appointed Cao Cao to act as Governor of Ji Province;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an imperial edict made Cao Cao Governor of Ji Province;

sentences.zh: 操讓還兗州。

translations.literal: Cao Cao declined and remained Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao declined and kept only Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 初，袁尚遣從事安平牽招至上黨督軍糧，未還，尚走中山，招說高幹以并州迎尚，並力觀變，幹不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Shang had sent Aide Qian Zhao of Anping to Shangdang to supervise military grain; before he returned, Shang fled to Zhongshan; Zhao tried to persuade Gao Gan to use Bing Province to welcome Shang and watch developments together with united strength — Gan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Shang had sent Qian Zhao of Anping to Shangdang to oversee military supplies. Before Zhao returned, Shang fled to Zhongshan. Zhao urged Gao Gan to bring Bing Province to Shang's aid and wait to see how things developed, but Gan refused.

sentences.zh: 招乃東詣曹操，操復以為冀州從事。

translations.literal: Zhao then went east to Cao Cao, and Cao Cao again appointed him Aide of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then went east to Cao Cao, who appointed him an aide in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 又辟崔琰為別駕，操謂琰曰：「昨案戶籍，可得三十萬眾，故為大州也。

translations.literal: He also summoned Cui Yan as Registrar; Cao Cao said to Yan: "Yesterday I examined the household registers — I could get three hundred thousand persons; therefore this is a great province."
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited Cui Yan as Registrar. Cao Cao told him, "Yesterday I reviewed the household registers. This province can field three hundred thousand men. A great province indeed."

sentences.zh: 」琰對曰：「今九州幅裂，二袁兄弟親尋干戈，冀方蒸庶，暴骨原野，未聞王師存問風俗，救其塗炭，而校計甲兵，唯此為先，斯豈鄙州士女所望於明公哉！

translations.literal: " Yan replied: "Now the Nine Provinces are split asunder; the two Yuan brothers personally seek battle with one another; the common people of Ji are strewn dead on the wild fields — one has not heard that the royal army inquires after local custom and saves them from drowning in fire and water, yet you tally soldiers and armor and put this first — is this what the gentlemen and ladies of this humble province hope for from Your Excellency!"
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Yan answered, "The empire is torn apart. The Yuan brothers war with each other while Ji Province's people die in the fields. No one has heard of the court asking after their welfare or lifting them from misery, yet you count first how many soldiers you can raise. Is that what this province expects of you?"

sentences.zh: 」操改容謝之。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao changed expression and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao's face changed and he apologized.

sentences.zh: 許攸恃功驕嫚，嘗於眾坐呼操小字曰：「某甲，卿非我，不得冀州也！

translations.literal: Xu You relied on his merit and was arrogant and insolent; once in a public gathering he called Cao Cao by his childhood name: "So-and-so — without me, you could not have gotten Ji Province!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu You grew proud of his service. Once at a public gathering he called Cao Cao by his childhood name: "Ah Man — without me, you'd never have taken Ji Province!"

sentences.zh: 」操笑曰：「汝言是也。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao laughed and said: "What you say is correct."
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao laughed and said, "You're right."

sentences.zh: 」然內不樂，後竟殺之。

translations.literal: " Yet inwardly he was displeased, and in the end he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " But inwardly he resented it, and in the end had Xu You killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，有星孛於東井。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, a comet appeared in the Well [constellation].
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, a comet appeared in the Well constellation.

sentences.zh: 高幹以并州降，操復以幹為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Gan submitted Bing Province and surrendered; Cao Cao again appointed Gan Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan surrendered Bing Province, and Cao Cao restored him as its governor.

sentences.zh: 曹操之圍鄴也，袁譚復背之，略取甘陵、安平、勃海、河間。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao was besieging Ye, Yuan Tan again turned against him, raiding and taking Ganling, Anping, Bohai, and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao besieged Ye, Yuan Tan turned on him again and seized Ganling, Anping, Bohai, and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 攻袁尚於中山，尚敗，走故安，從袁熙；

translations.literal: He attacked Yuan Shang at Zhongshan; Shang was defeated and fled to Gu'an, following Yuan Xi;
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yuan Shang at Zhongshan. Shang was defeated and fled with Yuan Xi to Gu'an;

sentences.zh: 譚悉收其眾，還屯龍湊。

translations.literal: Tan took in all his forces and returned to encamp at Longcou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan absorbed Shang's scattered troops and withdrew to Longcou.

sentences.zh: 操與譚書，責以負約，與之絕婚，女還，然後進討。

translations.literal: Cao Cao wrote to Tan, reproaching him for breaking the agreement, broke off the marriage alliance, sent the daughter back, and then advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote to rebuke Tan for breaking faith, annulled the marriage alliance and sent his son's betrothed home, then marched against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，操軍其門，譚拔平原，走保南皮，臨清河而屯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Cao Cao brought his army to Tan's gate; Tan abandoned Pingyuan, fled to hold Nanpi, and encamped on the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cao Cao attacked Tan at his gates. Tan abandoned Pingyuan, fled to Nanpi, and made camp on the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 操入平原，略定諸縣。

translations.literal: Cao Cao entered Pingyuan and pacified the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao entered Pingyuan and secured its counties.

sentences.zh: 曹操表公孫度為武威將軍，封永寧鄉侯。

translations.literal: Cao Cao memorialized that Gongsun Du be made General Who Manifests Martiality and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongning Township.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recommended Gongsun Du for the title General Who Manifests Martiality and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yongning Township.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「我王遼東，何永寧也！

translations.literal: Du said: "I am king of Liaodong — what is Yongning!"
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "I am king of Liaodong — what do I want with Yongning?"

sentences.zh: 」藏印綬於武庫。

translations.literal: " He stored the seal and ribbon in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: " He put the seal and ribbon away in the armory.

sentences.zh: 是歲，度卒，子康嗣位，以永寧鄉侯封其弟恭。

translations.literal: That year Du died; his son Kang succeeded to the position, and Yongning Township Marquis was used to enfeoff his younger brother Gong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gongsun Du died. His son Kang succeeded him, and Kang used the marquisate of Yongning to enfeoff his brother Gong.

sentences.zh: 操以牽招嘗為袁氏領烏桓，遣詣柳城，撫慰烏桓。

translations.literal: Because Qian Zhao had once led the Wuhuan for the Yuans, Cao Cao sent him to Liucheng to comfort and reassure the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qian Zhao had once commanded the Wuhuan for the Yuans, Cao Cao sent him to Liucheng to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 值峭王嚴五千騎欲助袁譚，又，公孫康遣使韓忠假峭王單于印綬。

translations.literal: It happened that Qiao Wang had five thousand horsemen wishing to aid Yuan Tan; moreover, Gongsun Kang sent his envoy Han Zhong to confer on Qiao Wang the seal and ribbon of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Wang had five thousand cavalry ready to aid Yuan Tan, and Gongsun Kang sent his envoy Han Zhong to invest Qiao Wang with the chanyu's seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 峭王大會群長，忠亦在坐。

translations.literal: Qiao Wang held a great assembly of the chieftains; Zhong was also seated there.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Wang summoned all the chieftains to a council; Han Zhong was present.

sentences.zh: 峭王問招：「昔袁公言受天子之命，假我為單于；

translations.literal: Qiao Wang asked Zhao: "Formerly Lord Yuan said he received the Son of Heaven's command and provisionally made me Chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Wang asked Qian Zhao, "Lord Yuan once said he had the emperor's authority and made me chanyu;

sentences.zh: 今曹公復言當更白天子，假我真單于；

translations.literal: Now Lord Cao again says he should report anew to the Son of Heaven and provisionally make me True Chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: now Lord Cao says he too will report to the emperor and make me true chanyu;

sentences.zh: 遼東復持印綬來。

translations.literal: Liaodong again brings seal and ribbon here.
translations.idiomatic: and now Liaodong brings another seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 如此，誰當為正？

translations.literal: In this way, who ought to be authoritative?"
translations.idiomatic: Who speaks with real authority?"

sentences.zh: 」招答曰：「昔袁公承製，得有所拜假。

translations.literal: " Zhao replied: "Formerly Lord Yuan received the imperial writ and could grant appointments and provisional titles."
translations.idiomatic: " Qian Zhao answered, "Lord Yuan held imperial authority and could confer titles.

sentences.zh: 中間違錯天子命，曹公代之，言當白天子，更假真單于，是也。

translations.literal: In the middle he erred against the Son of Heaven's command; Lord Cao replaced him — saying he should report to the Son of Heaven and renew the provisional grant of True Chanyu — that is correct.
translations.idiomatic: He then defied the emperor. Lord Cao replaced him and will report to the throne and confer the true chanyu's seal. That is the one to heed.

sentences.zh: 遼東下郡，何得擅稱拜假也！

translations.literal: Liaodong is a subordinate commandery — how could it on its own authority grant appointments and provisional titles!"
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong is only a commandery. What right has it to hand out titles on its own?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「我遼東在滄海之東，擁兵百餘萬，又有扶餘、濊貊之用。

translations.literal: " Zhong said: "Our Liaodong lies east of the blue sea; we hold more than a million troops, and moreover have the use of Buyeo and the Hui and Mo."
translations.idiomatic: " Han Zhong said, "Liaodong lies beyond the eastern sea. We command more than a million men and have Buyeo and the Mo tribes at our call.

sentences.zh: 當今之勢，強者為右，曹操何得獨為是也！

translations.literal: In the present situation, the strong take precedence — why should Cao Cao alone be authoritative!"
translations.idiomatic: In today's world, might makes right. Why should Cao Cao alone have the final say?"

sentences.zh: 」招呵忠曰：「曹公允恭明哲，翼戴天子，伐叛柔服，寧靜四海。

translations.literal: " Zhao shouted at Zhong: "Lord Cao is fair, respectful, enlightened, and wise; he supports and bears up the Son of Heaven, punishes rebels and softens those who submit, and brings peace to the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: " Qian Zhao rebuked Han Zhong: "Lord Cao is fair, wise, and loyal to the throne. He crushes rebels and wins over the obedient and brings peace to the empire."

sentences.zh: 汝君臣頑囂，今恃險遠，背違天命，欲擅拜假，侮弄神器；

translations.literal: You, lord and ministers, are stubborn and insolent; now relying on perilous distance, you disobey Heaven's mandate, wish on your own authority to grant appointments and provisional titles, and mock and play with the imperial regalia;
translations.idiomatic: You lord and subject are stubborn and arrogant. Sheltered by your distant stronghold, you defy Heaven's mandate, hand out titles on your own authority, and trifle with the symbols of imperial power;

sentences.zh: 方當屠戮，何敢慢易咎毀大人！

translations.literal: You are about to be slaughtered — how dare you slight and revile the great man!
translations.idiomatic: Your turn for the blade is coming — how dare you slight and insult Lord Cao!

sentences.zh: 」便捉忠頭頓築，拔刀欲斬之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon seized Zhong's head and beat it against the floor, drew his sword, and wished to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: " He grabbed Han Zhong by the head and slammed it against the floor, then drew his sword to kill him.

sentences.zh: 峭王驚怖，徒跣抱招，以救請忠，左右失色。

translations.literal: Qiao Wang was terrified; barefoot, he embraced Zhao to plead for Zhong's life, and those on either side lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Wang was terrified. Barefoot, he threw his arms around Qian Zhao and begged him to spare Han Zhong; everyone present went pale.

sentences.zh: 招乃還坐，為峭王等說成敗之效，禍福所歸；

translations.literal: Zhao then returned to his seat and for Qiao Wang and the others explained the effects of success and failure and where fortune and disaster lie;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao resumed his seat and explained to Qiao Wang and the rest what victory and defeat meant and where blessing and ruin would fall;

sentences.zh: 皆下席跪伏，敬受敕教，便辭遼東之使，罷所嚴騎。

translations.literal: All left their seats, knelt and prostrated themselves, reverently received his instructions, then dismissed the Liaodong envoy and disbanded the cavalry they had assembled.
translations.idiomatic: All rose from their seats, knelt in submission, and accepted his counsel. They sent the Liaodong envoy away and stood down the cavalry they had mustered.

sentences.zh: 丹楊大都督媯覽、郡丞戴員殺太守孫翊。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant of Danyang Gui Lan and the Assistant Administrator Dai Yuan killed the Administrator Sun Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Lan, Grand Commandant of Danyang, and Dai Yuan, the assistant administrator, murdered the prefect Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 將軍孫河屯京城，馳赴宛陵，覽、員復殺之；

translations.literal: General Sun He was encamped at Jingcheng; he galloped to Wanling, and Lan and Yuan killed him as well;
translations.idiomatic: General Sun He was stationed at Jingcheng. He raced to Wanling, but Lan and Yuan killed him too;

sentences.zh: 遣人迎揚州刺史劉馥，令往歷陽，以丹楊應之。

translations.literal: They sent men to welcome Inspector of Yang Province Liu Fu, ordering him to go to Liyang so that Danyang could respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: They sent for Liu Fu, inspector of Yang Province, and summoned him to Liyang to rally Danyang to their cause.

sentences.zh: 覽入居軍府中，欲逼取翊妻徐氏。

translations.literal: Lan entered and took up residence in the military headquarters, wishing to force Sun Yi's wife, Lady Xu, to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Lan moved into the military headquarters and tried to take Sun Yi's wife, Lady Xu, by force.

sentences.zh: 徐氏紿之曰：「乞須晦日，設祭除服，然後聽命。

translations.literal: Lady Xu deceived him, saying: "I beg to wait until the last day of mourning, set up offerings and remove mourning garb, and then obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu deceived him. "Please grant me until the last day of mourning," she said. "Let me perform the final rites and lay aside my mourning robes, and then I will submit.

sentences.zh: 」覽許之。

translations.literal: " Lan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Lan agreed.

sentences.zh: 徐氏潛使所親語翊親近舊將孫高、傅嬰等與共圖覽，高、嬰涕泣許諾，密呼翊時侍養者二十餘人與盟誓合謀。

translations.literal: Lady Xu secretly had a close confidant speak with Sun Yi's former intimate old generals Sun Gao, Fu Ying, and the others to plot Lan's death together; Gao and Ying wept and promised, secretly summoning more than twenty of Sun Yi's former attendants to swear an oath and join the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu secretly sent a trusted attendant to Sun Gao, Fu Ying, and other of Sun Yi's old officers to plot Gui Lan's death. Gao and Ying wept as they pledged themselves, and in secret they gathered more than twenty of Sun Yi's former servants to swear an oath and join the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 到晦日，設祭。

translations.literal: When the last day of mourning arrived, she set up the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When the last day of mourning came, she performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 徐氏哭泣盡哀，畢，乃除服，薰香沐浴，言笑歡悅。

translations.literal: Lady Xu wept to the full measure of grief; when finished, she removed mourning garb, burned incense and bathed, and spoke and laughed with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu wept until her grief was spent. Then she put off her mourning dress, bathed, scented herself, and appeared merry and laughing.

sentences.zh: 大小心妻愴，怪其如此。

translations.literal: Young and old alike were sorrowful at heart and found her behavior strange.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old in the household were heartsick and puzzled by her behavior.

sentences.zh: 覽密覘，無復疑意。

translations.literal: Lan secretly observed her and no longer harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Lan watched her in secret and no longer doubted her.

sentences.zh: 徐氏呼高、嬰置戶內，使人召覽入。

translations.literal: Lady Xu called Gao and Ying and placed them inside the door, then sent someone to summon Lan in.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu hid Sun Gao and Fu Ying inside, then sent for Gui Lan.

sentences.zh: 徐氏出戶拜覽，適得一拜，徐大呼：「二君可起！

translations.literal: Lady Xu came out and bowed to Lan; just as she had completed one bow, Xu shouted loudly: "You two gentlemen, rise!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu came out to greet him with a bow. At the very moment she rose from her first obeisance, she cried, "Now, you two — rise!"

sentences.zh: 」高、嬰俱出，共殺覽，餘人即就外殺員。

translations.literal: " Gao and Ying both came out together and jointly killed Lan; the others immediately went outside and killed Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao and Ying burst out and killed Lan. The rest rushed outside and killed Dai Yuan.

sentences.zh: 徐氏乃還縗絲至，奉覽、員首以祭翊墓，舉軍震駭。

translations.literal: Lady Xu then put on hemp mourning garb again; she presented the heads of Lan and Yuan to sacrifice at Sun Yi's tomb, and the whole army was shaken with awe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu put her mourning dress back on, offered Lan's and Yuan's heads at Sun Yi's tomb, and the whole army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 孫權聞亂，從椒丘還。

translations.literal: Sun Quan heard of the disorder and returned from Jiaoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan heard of the uprising, he returned from Jiaoqiu.

sentences.zh: 至丹楊，悉族誅覽、員餘黨，擢高、嬰為牙門，其餘賞賜有差。

translations.literal: When he reached Danyang, he utterly exterminated the remaining partisans of Lan and Yuan by clan punishment, promoted Gao and Ying to commanders of the corps, and gave the others rewards according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Danyang, he wiped out the remaining Lan and Yuan factions to the last clan, promoted Sun Gao and Fu Ying to gate commanders, and rewarded the others according to their service.

sentences.zh: 河子韶，年十七，收河餘眾屯京城。

translations.literal: He's son Shao, seventeen years old, gathered He's remaining troops and encamped at Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He's son Shao, seventeen, gathered his father's remaining troops and held Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 權引軍發吳，夜至京城下營，試攻驚之；

translations.literal: Quan led his army forth from Wu, at night reached Jingcheng and encamped below it, and made a trial attack to startle them;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan marched from Wu and by night encamped below Jingcheng, testing the garrison with a surprise attack;

sentences.zh: 兵皆乘城，傳檄備警，歡聲動地，頗射外人。

translations.literal: The troops all mounted the walls, circulated proclamations and stood on alert; shouts of joy shook the earth, and they shot somewhat at outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders manned the walls, circulated proclamations, and raised a cheer that shook the ground. Some even shot at Sun Quan's men outside.

sentences.zh: 權使曉諭，乃止。

translations.literal: Quan sent men to explain and reassure them, and they then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent envoys to explain, and the commotion ceased.

sentences.zh: 明日見韶，拜承列校尉，統河部曲。

translations.literal: The next day he met Shao, invested him as Colonel of the Successive Array, and put him in command of He's former troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he received Shao, appointed him Colonel of the Successive Array, and put him in command of Sun He's old company.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹操攻南皮，袁譚出戰，士卒多死。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao attacked Nanpi; Yuan Tan went out to battle, and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao attacked Nanpi. Yuan Tan met him in battle, and many of his men fell.

sentences.zh: 操欲緩之，議郎曹純曰：「今縣師深入，難以持久，若進不能克，退必喪威。

translations.literal: Cao wished to slacken the attack; Master of Proposals Cao Chun said: "Now the army hangs deep in enemy territory and cannot be sustained long; if we advance and cannot take it, retreat will surely lose prestige."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wanted to ease off. Cao Chun, Master of Proposals, said, "Our army is far inside hostile country and cannot linger. If we press on and fail, or withdraw, we lose face either way."

sentences.zh: 」乃自執桴鼓以率攻者，遂克之。

translations.literal: " He then personally took the drumstick and drum to lead the attackers, and thereby took the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He took up drum and mallet himself, led the assault, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 譚出走，追斬之。

translations.literal: Tan fled; they pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan fled. Pursuers ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 李孚自稱冀州主簿，求見操曰：「今城中弱強相陵，人心擾亂，以為宜令新降為內所識信者宣傳明教。

translations.literal: Li Fu styled himself Chief Clerk of Ji Province, sought audience with Cao Cao, and said: "Now within the city the weak and strong bully one another and hearts are disturbed; I think it fitting to have newly surrendered men known and trusted within be sent to proclaim the clear instructions."
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, calling himself chief clerk of Ji Province, asked to see Cao Cao. "The strong are preying on the weak inside the city and the people are panicking," he said. "Send in someone the garrison knows and trusts among the recent surrenderers to proclaim your orders."

sentences.zh: 」操即使孚往入城，告諭吏民，使各安故業，不得相侵，城中乃安。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao thereupon sent Fu into the city to announce and instruct officials and commoners, ordering each to keep to his former occupation and not encroach on one another, and the city thereby became settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao sent Li Fu into the city to reassure officials and commoners, telling each to keep to his trade and leave his neighbors unmolested. The city calmed.

sentences.zh: 操於是斬郭圖等及其妻子。

translations.literal: Cao Cao thereupon beheaded Guo Tu and the others, together with their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then executed Guo Tu and his followers, along with their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 袁譚使王修運糧於樂安，聞譚急，將所領兵往赴之，至高密，聞譚死，下馬號哭曰：「無君焉歸！

translations.literal: Yuan Tan had sent Wang Xiu to transport grain at Le'an; hearing Tan was in peril, he led the troops under his command to go to his aid; reaching Gaomi, he heard Tan was dead, dismounted, and wailed aloud: "Without my lord, whither shall I return!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan had sent Wang Xiu to convoy grain at Le'an. When Wang Xiu heard that Tan was in peril, he marched to his relief. At Gaomi he learned Tan was dead, dismounted, and wailed, "My lord is gone — where shall I go?"

sentences.zh: 」遂諧曹操，乞收葬譚屍，操許之，復使修還樂安，督軍糧。

translations.literal: " He then went to Cao Cao and begged leave to gather and bury Tan's corpse; Cao Cao agreed and again sent Xiu back to Le'an to oversee army grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to Cao Cao and asked permission to bury Tan's body. Cao Cao agreed and sent Wang Xiu back to Le'an to oversee the army's grain supply.

sentences.zh: 譚所部諸城皆服，唯樂安太守管統不下。

translations.literal: All the cities under Tan's command submitted; only Le'an Administrator Guan Tong would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Every city in Tan's orbit submitted except Le'an, where the prefect Guan Tong refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 操命修取統首，修以統亡國忠臣，解其縛，使詣操，操悅而赦之，辟修為司空掾。

translations.literal: Cao Cao ordered Xiu to bring Tong's head; Xiu, considering Tong a loyal minister of a fallen state, released his bonds and had him go to Cao Cao; Cao Cao was pleased and pardoned him, and recruited Xiu as an aide in the Department of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ordered Wang Xiu to bring him Guan Tong's head. Wang Xiu, deeming Tong a loyal man of a fallen house, freed him and sent him to Cao Cao. Cao Cao was pleased and spared him, and took Wang Xiu onto his staff in the Department of Works.

sentences.zh: 郭嘉說操多辟青、冀、幽、并名士以為掾屬，使人心歸附，操從之。

translations.literal: Guo Jia urged Cao Cao to recruit many famous scholars of Qing, Ji, You, and Bing as aides and staff, so that hearts would turn and attach; Cao Cao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia urged Cao Cao to recruit distinguished men from Qing, Ji, You, and Bing as aides so that the people would rally to him. Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 官渡之戰，袁紹使陳琳為檄書，數操罪惡，連及家世，極其醜詆。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Guandu, Yuan Shao had Chen Lin compose a proclamation listing Cao Cao's crimes, extending to his family and lineage, vilifying him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu, Yuan Shao had Chen Lin draft a proclamation listing Cao Cao's crimes, dragging in his whole lineage and heaping abuse upon him.

sentences.zh: 及袁氏敗，琳歸操，操曰：「卿昔為本初移書，但可罪狀孤身，何乃上及父祖邪！

translations.literal: When the Yuans were defeated, Lin came over to Cao Cao; Cao Cao said: "You formerly wrote for Benchu a letter of transfer — it would have been enough to charge my person alone with crimes; why reach upward to my father and grandfather!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan clan fell, Chen Lin surrendered to Cao Cao. Cao Cao said, "When you wrote that tract for Shao, you might have condemned me alone. Why drag in my father and grandfather?"

sentences.zh: 」琳謝罪，操釋之，使與陳留阮瑀俱管記室。

translations.literal: " Lin asked forgiveness; Cao Cao released him and had him together with Chenliu Ruan Yu jointly manage the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Lin apologized. Cao Cao pardoned him and put him and Ruan Yu of Chenliu in charge of his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是漁陽王松據涿郡，郡人劉放說松以地歸操，操辟放參司空軍事。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Song of Fuyang held Zhuo Commandery; a man of the commandery, Liu Fang, persuaded Song to surrender the territory to Cao Cao; Cao Cao recruited Fang to participate in the Department of Works' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Song of Fuyang had held Zhuo Commandery. Liu Fang, a local man, persuaded him to surrender to Cao Cao, and Cao Cao took Liu Fang onto his military staff in the Department of Works.

sentences.zh: 袁熙為其將焦觸、張南所攻，與尚俱奔遼西烏桓。

translations.literal: Yuan Xi was attacked by his generals Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan; he and Shang both fled to the Liaoxi Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi's own generals Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan turned on him. He and Yuan Shang fled to the Liaoxi Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 觸自號幽州刺史，驅率諸郡太守令長，背袁向曹，陳兵數萬，殺白馬而盟，令曰：「敢違者斬！

translations.literal: Chu styled himself Inspector of You Province, drove and led the grand administrators, prefects, and magistrates of the various commanderies, turned from the Yuans toward Cao, arrayed tens of thousands of troops, killed a white horse to swear the oath, and commanded: "Whoever dares disobey shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chu styled himself inspector of You Province, rallied the prefects and magistrates of the commanderies, and defected from the Yuans to Cao Cao. He mustered tens of thousands of men, sacrificed a white horse, and swore them to the oath: "Whoever defies this oath dies!"

sentences.zh: 」眾莫敢仰視，各以次歃。

translations.literal: " None of the multitude dared look up; each in order drank the blood.
translations.idiomatic: " None dared meet his eye. One by one they drank the oath.

sentences.zh: 別駕代郡韓珩曰：「吾受袁公父子厚恩，今其破亡，智不能救，勇不能死，於義闕矣。

translations.literal: Attendant Administrator Han Heng of Dai Commandery said: "I received thick kindness from Lord Yuan father and son; now that they are destroyed and ruined, in wisdom I could not rescue them, in courage I could not die — in righteousness I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: Han Heng, attendant administrator of Dai, said, "The Yuan father and son showed me great kindness. Their house is ruined. I lacked the wit to save them and the courage to die with them. In duty I already fail."

sentences.zh: 若乃北面曹氏，所不能為也。

translations.literal: If I am to turn north and face the Cao clan, that is what I cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: But to bow to the Cao clan — that I cannot do."

sentences.zh: 」一坐為珩失色。

translations.literal: " The whole assembly changed color at Heng.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole company turned pale.

sentences.zh: 觸曰：「夫舉大事，當立大義，事之濟否，不待一人，可卒珩志，以厲事君。

translations.literal: Chu said: "In undertaking great affairs, one ought to establish great righteousness; whether the affair succeeds or not does not depend on one man — one may fulfill Heng's wish to the end, to encourage service to one's lord."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chu said, "Great undertakings rest on great principle. Success does not hinge on one man. Let us honor Han Heng's wish and make an example of loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」乃捨之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: " He spared him.

sentences.zh: 觸等遂降曹操，皆封為列侯。

translations.literal: Chu and the others thereupon submitted to Cao Cao and were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chu and his companions surrendered to Cao Cao and were all enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，黑山賊帥張燕率其眾十餘萬降，封安國亭侯。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, bandit chief of the Black Mountains Zhang Yan led his following of more than a hundred thousand to submit; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Village.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhang Yan, chieftain of the Black Mountain bandits, surrendered with more than a hundred thousand followers and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Village.

sentences.zh: 故安趙犢、霍奴等殺幽州刺史及涿郡太守，三郡烏桓攻鮮于輔於獷平。

translations.literal: Zhao Du of Gu'an, Huo Nu, and the others killed the Inspector of You Province and the Administrator of Zhuo Commandery; Wuhuan of three commanderies attacked Xianyu Fu at Kuangping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Du of Gu'an, Huo Nu, and others murdered the inspector of You Province and the prefect of Zhuo. Wuhuan from three commanderies attacked Xianyu Fu at Kuangping.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，操討犢等，斬之；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, Cao Cao campaigned against Du and the others and beheaded them;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Cao Cao marched against Zhao Du and his band and executed them;

sentences.zh: 乃渡潞水救獷平，烏桓走出塞。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Lu River to rescue Kuangping; the Wuhuan fled out of the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: then crossed the Lu River to relieve Kuangping. The Wuhuan fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，高幹聞操討烏桓，復以并州叛，執上黨太守，舉兵守壺關口。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Gao Gan heard Cao Cao was campaigning against the Wuhuan and again rebelled with Bing Province, seized the Administrator of Shangdang, and raised troops to hold Huguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, hearing that Cao Cao was off fighting the Wuhuan, Gao Gan rebelled again in Bing Province, seized the prefect of Shangdang, and raised troops to hold Huguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 操遣其將樂進、李典擊之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent his generals Yue Jin and Li Dian to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Yue Jin and Li Dian against him.

sentences.zh: 河內張晟，眾萬餘人，寇崤、澠間，弘農張琰起兵以應之。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng of Henei, with a following of more than ten thousand, raided between Xiao and Mian; Zhang Yan of Hongnong raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng of Henei, with more than ten thousand men, raided between the Xiao and Mian passes. Zhang Yan of Hongnong took up arms in support.

sentences.zh: 河東太守王邑被征，郡掾衛固及中郎將范先等詣司隸校尉鐘繇，請留之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Hedong Wang Yi was summoned; the commandery clerk Wei Gu and the General of the Gentlemen of the Household Fan Xian and others went to the Director of Retainers Zhong Yao and asked that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Hedong, Wang Yi, was called to court. Wei Gu, a commandery clerk, and Fan Xian, a general of the household, went to Zhong Yao, director of retainers, and asked that Wang Yi be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 繇不許。

translations.literal: Yao did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao refused.

sentences.zh: 固等外以請邑為名，而內實與高幹通牒。

translations.literal: Gu and the others outwardly took requesting Yi as their pretext, but inwardly were in fact exchanging messages with Gao Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Wei Gu and his allies pleaded for Wang Yi; inwardly they were already in league with Gao Gan.

sentences.zh: 曹操謂荀彧曰：「關西諸將，外服內貳，張晟寇亂殽、澠，南通劉表，固等因之，將為深害。

translations.literal: Cao Cao said to Xun Yu: "The generals west of the Pass outwardly submit but inwardly are divided; Zhang Sheng raids and disorders Xiao and Mian, links south to Liu Biao, and Gu and the others follow upon this — they will become a deep harm."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told Xun Yu, "The generals west of the Pass bow on the surface but waver within. Zhang Sheng is ravaging the Xiao and Mian region and reaching south toward Liu Biao. With Wei Gu and the rest stirring trouble, the danger runs deep.

sentences.zh: 當今河東，天下之要地也，君為我舉賢才以鎮之。

translations.literal: Hedong today is a crucial place of the empire; please recommend worthy talent for me to secure it."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong is a pivot of the realm. Find me a worthy man to hold it."

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「西平太守京兆杜畿，勇足以當難，智足以應變。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Administrator of Xiping Du Ji of Jingzhao — courage enough to meet hardship, wisdom enough to respond to change."
translations.idiomatic: " Xun Yu said, "Du Ji of Jingzhao, prefect of Xiping — brave enough to face crisis, shrewd enough to adapt."

sentences.zh: 」操乃以畿為河東太守。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao thereupon made Ji Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao appointed Du Ji prefect of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 鐘繇促王邑交符，邑佩印綬，逕從河北詣許自歸。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao pressed Wang Yi to hand over the seal and ribbon; Yi wore the seal and ribbon on his belt and went straight from Hebei to Xu to surrender himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao pressed Wang Yi to surrender his seal of office. Yi took the insignia and went straight from Hebei to Xu to submit in person.

sentences.zh: 衛固等使兵數千人絕陝津，杜畿至，數月不得渡。

translations.literal: Wei Gu and the others sent several thousand troops to block Shan Pass crossing; Du Ji arrived but for several months could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu sent several thousand men to block the Shan Pass ford. Du Ji arrived but could not cross for months.

sentences.zh: 操遣夏侯惇討固等，未至，畿曰：「河東有三萬戶，非皆欲為亂也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Dun to campaign against Gu and the others; before he arrived, Ji said: "Hedong has thirty thousand households — not all wish to make rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dispatched Xiahou Dun to crush Wei Gu. Before he arrived, Du Ji said, "Hedong has thirty thousand households. Not all of them want rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今兵迫之急，欲為善者無主，必懼而聽於固。

translations.literal: Now with troops pressing them urgently, those who wish to do good have no leader and will surely, in fear, obey Gu.
translations.idiomatic: But with an army at the gates, good men have no one to follow. In fear they will fall in behind Wei Gu.

sentences.zh: 固等勢專，必以死戰。

translations.literal: Gu and the others hold sole power and will surely fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu will hold the field and fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 討之不勝，為難未已；

translations.literal: If we campaign against them and do not prevail, the trouble will not end;
translations.idiomatic: Defeat him and the trouble persists;

sentences.zh: 討之而勝，是殘一郡之民也。

translations.literal: if we campaign against them and prevail, that is to mutilate the people of a whole commandery.
translations.idiomatic: victory means slaughtering a whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 且固等未顯絕王命，外以請故君為名，必不害新君。

translations.literal: Moreover, Gu and the others have not openly renounced the royal command; outwardly they take petitioning the former lord as their name — they will surely not harm the new lord.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Wei Gu has not openly defied the throne. He only claims to be pleading for the old prefect. He will not dare kill the new one.

sentences.zh: 吾單車直往，出其不意，固為人多計而無斷，必偽受吾。

translations.literal: If I go alone in a single carriage straight there, catching them unawares, Gu is a man of many schemes but no resolution — he will surely feign acceptance of me.
translations.idiomatic: If I ride in alone and take them by surprise, Wei Gu — crafty but indecisive — will pretend to accept me.

sentences.zh: 吾得居郡一月，以計縻之，足矣。

translations.literal: If I can remain in the commandery one month and hold them with stratagem, that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Give me a month in office to tie his hands, and that will be enough."

sentences.zh: 」遂詭道從郖津度。

translations.literal: " He thereupon took a roundabout route and crossed by Xi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: " He took a roundabout route and crossed at Xi Ford.

sentences.zh: 范先欲殺畿以威眾，且觀畿去就，於門下斬殺主簿已下三十餘人，畿舉動自若。

translations.literal: Fan Xian wished to kill Ji to overawe the multitude and also to observe Ji's course; at the gate he beheaded the chief clerk and more than thirty men below that rank; Ji moved and acted as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xian meant to kill Du Ji to cow the rest and test his resolve. At the gate he beheaded the chief clerk and more than thirty subordinates. Du Ji did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 於是固曰：「殺之無損，徒有惡名；

translations.literal: Thereupon Gu said: "Killing him does no good and only brings a bad name;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu said, "Killing him gains us nothing and wins us infamy;

sentences.zh: 且制之在我。

translations.literal: moreover, controlling him lies with us."
translations.idiomatic: and we hold him in our power anyway."

sentences.zh: 」遂奉之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon received and served him.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted Du Ji as prefect.

sentences.zh: 畿謂固、先曰：「衛、范，河東之望也，吾仰成而已。

translations.literal: Ji said to Gu and Xian: "Wei and Fan are the hopes of Hedong; I rely on your completion, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji told Wei Gu and Fan Xian, "You two are the pillars of Hedong. I mean only to lean on your support.

sentences.zh: 然君固有定義，成敗同之，大事當共平議。

translations.literal: Yet you, lords, surely have settled righteousness; success and failure are shared — great affairs ought to be jointly deliberated and settled."
translations.idiomatic: But you are men of principle. We rise or fall together. Weighty matters should be settled among us."

sentences.zh: 」以固為都督，行丞事，領功曹。

translations.literal: " He made Gu supervising commander, acting as deputy administrator, and head clerk for merit records.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Wei Gu supervising commander with acting deputy prefect's duties and put him in charge of the merit clerk's office.

sentences.zh: 將校吏兵三千餘人，皆范先督之。

translations.literal: More than three thousand officers, clerks, soldiers, and troops — all were supervised by Fan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand officers and men were placed under Fan Xian's command.

sentences.zh: 固等喜，雖陽事畿，不以為意。

translations.literal: Gu and the others were pleased; though outwardly they served Ji, they did not take him seriously.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu and his allies were delighted. They paid Du Ji lip service and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 固欲大發兵，畿患之，說固曰：「今大發兵，眾情必擾，不如徐以貲募兵。

translations.literal: Gu wished to raise a great army; Ji was troubled by this and said to Gu: "Now if you raise a great army, the multitude's hearts will surely be disturbed — better to raise troops slowly with money and goods."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu wanted to mobilize a large force. Du Ji objected. "A mass levy will panic the people," he said. "Better to raise troops slowly with cash bounties."

sentences.zh: 」固以為然，從之，得兵甚少。

translations.literal: " Gu thought this correct, followed it, and obtained very few troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Gu agreed. He followed the advice and mustered only a handful of men.

sentences.zh: 畿又喻固等曰：「人情顧家，諸將掾史，可分遣休息，急緩召之不難。

translations.literal: Ji again instructed Gu and the others: "Human hearts care for home; the various generals and clerks can be sent off in groups to rest — in urgency or ease, summoning them back is not difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji urged Wei Gu again: "Men worry for their families. Send the officers and clerks home on leave — you can always call them back when needed."

sentences.zh: 」固等惡逆眾心，又從之。

translations.literal: " Gu and the others, though wicked and rebellious, bowed to popular hearts and again followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Gu, loath to alienate the people, agreed again.

sentences.zh: 於是善人在外，陰為己援；

translations.literal: Thereupon good men were outside, secretly forming support for themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Good men dispersed to the countryside and quietly rallied to Du Ji;

sentences.zh: 惡人分散，各還其家。

translations.literal: wicked men scattered, each returning to his home.
translations.idiomatic: the ringleaders scattered, each to his own home.

sentences.zh: 會白騎攻東垣，高幹入濩澤。

translations.literal: It happened that the White Horse cavalry attacked Dongyuan; Gao Gan entered Huo Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: About then the White Horse cavalry attacked Dongyuan and Gao Gan withdrew into Huo Marsh.

sentences.zh: 畿知諸縣附己，乃出，單將數十騎，赴堅壁而守之，吏民多舉城且畿者，比數十日，得四千餘人。

translations.literal: Ji knew the various counties attached themselves to him; he then went out, leading alone several dozen horsemen, went to a strong wall and held it; officials and commoners mostly raised cities and attached themselves to Ji — within about ten days he got more than four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the counties were declaring for him, Du Ji rode out with a few dozen horsemen, took a fortified position, and held it. Within ten days more than four thousand officials and commoners had rallied to his banner.

sentences.zh: 固等與高幹、張晟共攻畿，不下，略諸縣，無所得。

translations.literal: Gu and the others together with Gao Gan and Zhang Sheng jointly attacked Ji but could not take him; they raided the various counties and got nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gu, Gao Gan, and Zhang Sheng besieged him but could not break him. They pillaged the counties and gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 曹操使議郎張既西征關中諸將馬騰等，皆引兵會擊晟等，破之，斬固、琰等著，其餘黨與皆赦之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Master of Proposals Zhang Ji to campaign west against the generals west of the Pass Ma Teng and the others; all led troops to join in attacking Sheng and the others, defeated them, beheaded Gu, Yan, and the others as examples, and pardoned the rest of the partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Zhang Ji west against Ma Teng and the other Pass generals. They converged on Zhang Sheng, routed the rebels, executed Wei Gu and Zhang Yan as examples, and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 於是杜畿治河東，務崇寬惠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Du Ji governed Hedong, devoting himself to honoring leniency and beneficence.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji then governed Hedong with a policy of mercy and kindness.

sentences.zh: 民有辭訟，畿為陳義理，遣歸諦思之，父老皆自相責怒，不敢訟。

translations.literal: When commoners had lawsuits, Ji would explain the principles of right for them and send them home to ponder deeply; the elders all reproached and rebuked one another and did not bring suit.
translations.idiomatic: When people came with disputes, Du Ji would explain the rights of the matter and send them home to think it over. The village elders would rebuke one another and no one dared sue.

sentences.zh: 勸耕桑，課畜牧，百姓家家豐實。

translations.literal: He urged farming and mulberry culture, assessed livestock raising, and in every household the people were full and solid.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted farming and sericulture, encouraged livestock, and every household grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 然後興學校，舉孝弟，修戎事，講武備，河東遂安。

translations.literal: He then established schools, promoted filial piety and brotherly duty, repaired military affairs, and drilled martial readiness — and Hedong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He established schools, promoted filial piety and brotherly duty, trained the army, and drilled martial readiness — and Hedong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 畿在河東十六年，常為天下最。

translations.literal: Ji governed Hedong for sixteen years, and it was regularly ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ji governed Hedong for sixteen years, and it was regularly ranked the finest commandery in the realm.

sentences.zh: 秘書監、侍中荀悅作《申鑒》五篇，奏之。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant Xun Yue composed five chapters of the Shenjian and presented them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant Xun Yue composed five chapters of the Shenjian and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 悅，爽之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xun Yue was the son of Xun Shuang's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yue was a nephew of Xun Shuang.

sentences.zh: 時政在曹氏，天子恭己，悅志在獻替，而謀無所用，故作是書。

translations.literal: At the time political power lay with the Cao clan; the Son of Heaven held himself in respectful retirement. Xun Yue's intent was to offer remonstrance and replacement, but his plans had no outlet — therefore he composed this book.
translations.idiomatic: Political power lay with the Cao clan while the Son of Heaven held himself in respectful retirement. Xun Yue wished to offer counsel but had no avenue — therefore he wrote this book.

sentences.zh: 其大略曰：為政之術，先屏四患，乃崇五政。

translations.literal: Its general outline says: The art of governing lies first in barring the four harms, then in exalting the five policies.
translations.idiomatic: Its general argument runs: sound government must first eliminate four harms, then establish five policies.

sentences.zh: 偽亂欲，私壞法，放越軌，奢敗制：四者不除，則政末由行矣，是為四患。

translations.literal: Falsity disordering desire, selfishness ruining law, license overstepping norms, extravagance destroying institutions — if these four are not removed, government cannot be carried out; these are called the four harms.
translations.idiomatic: Falsity that disorders desire, selfishness that ruins law, license that oversteps norms, extravagance that destroys institutions — unless these four are removed, government cannot function. These are the four harms.

sentences.zh: 興農桑以養其生，審好惡以正其俗，宣文教以章其化，立武備以秉其威，明常罰以統其法，是謂五政。

translations.literal: Promote farming and sericulture to sustain their livelihood; examine likes and dislikes to rectify their customs; proclaim civil teaching to manifest their transformation; establish martial readiness to wield authority; clarify regular punishments to unify the law — these are called the five policies.
translations.idiomatic: Promote farming and sericulture to sustain livelihood; judge likes and dislikes to rectify custom; proclaim civil teaching to manifest transformation; establish martial readiness to wield authority; clarify regular punishments to unify law — these are the five policies.

sentences.zh: 人不畏死，不可懼以罪；

translations.literal: When people do not fear death, they cannot be frightened by punishment;
translations.idiomatic: When people do not fear death, punishment cannot frighten them;

sentences.zh: 人不樂生，不可勸以善。

translations.literal: when people do not delight in life, they cannot be urged toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: when people do not delight in life, goodness cannot win them over.

sentences.zh: 故在上者，先豐民財以定其志，是謂養生。

translations.literal: Therefore those above ought first to enrich the people's wealth to settle their wills — this is called sustaining life.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore rulers must first enrich the people's wealth to settle their minds — this is sustaining life.

sentences.zh: 善惡要乎功罪，毀譽效於准驗，聽言責事，舉名察實，無或作偽以蕩眾心。

translations.literal: Good and evil depend on merit and guilt; praise and blame take effect through verification; hear words but hold men to deeds; cite names but examine realities — let none manufacture falsity to unsettle the multitude's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil hinge on deeds; praise and blame require verification; heed words but judge by deeds; cite names but examine facts — let no one manufacture falsehood to unsettle the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 故欲無奸怪，民無淫風，是謂正俗。

translations.literal: Thus one desires no treachery or strangeness and the people have no licentious winds — this is called rectifying custom.
translations.idiomatic: Thus treachery is eliminated and licentious custom is checked — this is rectifying custom.

sentences.zh: 榮辱者，賞罰之精華也。

translations.literal: Honor and disgrace are the essence of reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Honor and disgrace are the essence of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 故禮教榮辱以加君子，化其情也；

translations.literal: Therefore ritual teaching applies honor and disgrace to gentlemen, transforming their feelings;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ritual teaching applies honor and disgrace to gentlemen, transforming their hearts;

sentences.zh: 桎梏鞭撲以加小人，化其形也。

translations.literal: fetters, cudgels, and floggings are applied to petty men, transforming their persons.
translations.idiomatic: fetters, cudgels, and floggings are applied to petty men, transforming their bodies.

sentences.zh: 若教化之廢，推中人而墜於小人之域，教化之行，引中人而納於君子之塗，是謂章化。

translations.literal: If civilizing transformation is abandoned, middling men are pushed down into the realm of petty men; if civilizing transformation is practiced, middling men are drawn up and brought into the path of gentlemen — this is called manifesting transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When civilizing transformation fails, ordinary men fall into petty ways; when it succeeds, ordinary men are drawn onto the path of gentlemen — this is manifesting transformation.

sentences.zh: 在上者必有武備以戒不虞，安居則寄之內政，有事則用之軍旅，是謂秉威。

translations.literal: Those above must have martial readiness to guard against the unforeseen; in peaceful dwelling they entrust it to civil government, in emergencies they employ it in the army — this is called wielding authority.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers must maintain martial readiness against the unforeseen — in peace entrust it to civil government, in crisis deploy it in the army. This is wielding authority.

sentences.zh: 賞罰，政之柄也。

translations.literal: Reward and punishment are the handles of government.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment are the handles of government.

sentences.zh: 人主不妄賞，非愛其財也，賞妄行，則善不勸矣；

translations.literal: The ruler does not reward rashly — not because he cherishes his wealth, but because rash rewarding will not encourage goodness;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler does not reward rashly — not from stinginess, but because rash rewards fail to encourage goodness;

sentences.zh: 不妄罰，非矜其人也，罰妄行，則惡不懲矣。

translations.literal: he does not punish rashly — not because he pities men, but because rash punishing will not chastise evil.
translations.idiomatic: nor punish rashly — not from pity, but because rash punishments fail to chastise evil.

sentences.zh: 賞不勸，謂之止善，罰不懲，謂之縱惡。

translations.literal: Reward that does not encourage is called halting goodness; punishment that does not chastise is called indulging evil.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards that do not encourage are called halting goodness; punishments that do not chastise are called indulging evil.

sentences.zh: 在上者能不止下為善，不縱下為惡，則國法立矣。

translations.literal: If those above can avoid halting subordinates in goodness and avoid indulging subordinates in evil, then the state's law is established.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers neither halt goodness below nor indulge evil below, the state's law stands firm.

sentences.zh: 是謂統法。

translations.literal: This is called unifying the law.
translations.idiomatic: This is unifying the law.

sentences.zh: 四患既蠲，五政又立，行之以誠，守之以固，簡而不怠，疏而不失，垂拱揖讓，而海內平矣。

translations.literal: Once the four harms are removed and the five policies established, practice them with sincerity, guard them with firmness, be simple without slackness, be sparse without loss — then, with folded hands and courteous yielding, the realm within the seas is pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Once the four harms are removed and the five policies established, practice them sincerely, guard them firmly, be simple without slackness, be sparing without neglect — and the realm is pacified while the ruler folds his hands in repose.
